text:
We've been building @jumperapp for over 3 years. 

Today, it has an established product and a user base that’s found value in our services.

And the numbers back that up:

- #1 aggregator by bridging volume.
- 15% market share in bridging.
- 100,000 monthly active users.
- Top 10 aggregators by swap volume.
- Go-to app for whales. 45% of the active addresses trade over $1k, $10k and $100k in size.

While this foundation is key, the next chapter of Jumper is about growing aggressively into different markets.

A few of our products that we believe will unlock the next levers of growth for Jumper:

- Jumper Advanced

1/3rd of Jumper’s volume ($~14.2B) is same chain swaps.

Same chain swaps are the highest onchain volume generating action (after perps), and it’s a service that we’ve consistently improved over the years.

Today, Jumper offers the best trade execution and feature set for same-chain swaps across 50+ chains - limit orders, TWAP, DCA, we’re bringing all the tools that a trader needs to win onchain.

The potential of doing this right and winning this market is 100x from here.

- Jumper Earn

We just hit $10M in attributed TVL on Jumper Earn last week.

The goal is to offer access to all yield opportunities across blockchains and make the UX for depositing/withdrawing from the vaults 1-click - removing all the other hassles.

It solves the yield discovery problem. And it removes the cross-chain complexity.

As DeFi TVL grows, the bet is that more of the deposit flows will come through Jumper.

- Jumper RWA

RWA / tokenized stocks volume onchain is still extremely early. But in the future, this category can grow 1000x as everything gets tokenized and more of stock trading comes onchain.

We shipped Jumper RWA - a trading interface that simplifies the onchain tokenised stock trading UX - with fragmentation across so many chains and issuers.

If tokenized stocks trading grows from here, which our bet is that it will, then Jumper RWA will be among the top places to trade them.

- Jumper Perps

Perps are one of the biggest drivers of onchain volume and arguably the market is extremely competitive and arguable saturated at this point.

We’re very aware of this fact and hence don’t want to bring another vanilla builder code integration to our users.

Jumper Perps is aggregation of perps trading venues - Hyperliquid, Lighter, and Ondo Perps to begin with.

To onboard the users on the platform, we will need to give them a reason to try out the platform. And this will come in the form of incentives, USD incentives and JUMP tokens - which we will bring with the underlying providers like Ondo.

And over time, we will ship more features and improvements that make the whole perps aggregation trading ux similar to what people expect on a swap/bridge aggregation level - abstract the complexity, compare the available venues, and execute orders through the best available paths.

The next chapter of Jumper is about giving our users more reasons to stay on Jumper, while at the same time, onboarding new users to the app - and get them to do more of their onchain activity through us.

We don’t need every one of these bets to become a massive market.

If we execute well, the markets are there for the taking and will be able to achieve our vision of making Jumper the super-app for onchain finance.

要突出这些特色：自动字幕、翻译、AI 配音、剪口癖、品牌套件、模板、动态贴纸与声波、智能裁剪、本地文生图、全部模型在本机跑、内置 Agent 复用本机的 Claude Code / Codex 等 CLI 而不需要 API key。

叙事：
图标拆开，星芒和播放头变成超级可爱的小机器人 Bao 手里的魔法棒，三条轨道拉长成时间轴，底板变成预览。Bao 给猫咪女主播 Mimi 的视频连施九段咒语（Subtitlio!、Translato!……），她说话时的 meow / purrr / nya~ 口癖变成小老鼠，被 Bao 一棒一个敲掉。

接着玻璃罩落下，表示「全部在你的 Mac 上跑」。最后一切倒带，Bao 敲碎 API key 输入框，一句话交给 Agent 全部做完，再把魔法棒插回图标。关键动作配震屏、冲击波和白闪。

DoubleZero runs on a more pure token economic model than most projects, and we've done a bunch of writing about this, but as there's a bunch of new people excited about the project, I thought I'd do a summary. 

DoubleZero is a protocol you can build anything on top of, but one of the most popular products developed is DoubleZero Edge. 

Edge works this way: 

- Fees are paid in stablecoin (or credit cards or ACH) and that swapped into  solana:J6pQQ3FAcJQeWPPGppWRb4nM8jU3wLyYbRrLh7feMfvd 

- 45% of that 2z is distributed to the fiber network providers that support the infrastructure network. Importantly, there are no passive emissions, so the only payout fiber contributors get is based on fees paid in. 

- 45% of that is distributed to the data originators, which in this case are participating Solana validators and Hyperliquid validators. These income streams are segmented by network (So Solana fees go to Solana validators, and Hyperliquid fees go to Hyperliquid validators.) 

- 10% of the solana:J6pQQ3FAcJQeWPPGppWRb4nM8jU3wLyYbRrLh7feMfvd is burned to permanently remove it from supply by destroying it.  

- The protocol has no inflation. 

DoubleZero.

Susquehanna is one of the most reputable trading firms in the world, and they make it mandatory that all their incoming traders learn poker.

I played in a game in NYC with a successful trader who came up there, and he described the scenario to me.

They literally had an entire floor of their office which was built into a poker room.

Every day at 4 pm, the new hires would go upstairs and play poker. The experienced traders would stop them mid hand and make them explain their decision making process.

Through poker they'd learn basic trading strategies such as risk/reward, odds, asymmetry and more, which they'd later use to trade millions on the options market.

Poker is one of life's greatest teachers, because both "games" contain imperfect information where the "players" go around making "bets" all day on what's about to happen.

text:
A humble attempt to est. the infra required to serve 100M DAU @Muse 

Rough conclusion is:

1 GW of power to serve 100M DAU in the base case, of which only ~0.1 GW comes from the CPU/VM layer. Depending on the # of reasoning-equivalent model calls one Muse DAU generates per day, 3-4GW is entirely plausible. Maybe that’s why @Meta  is rumored to be adding 7-10GW of compute next year.

The sandbox layer = sub $1B of CPU content and ~$2B of DRAM content, which is much smaller than many expected.

Lot of moving assumptions. Welcome all feedbacks/ pushbacks.

------
Two very different pieces of infrastructure behind Muse.

1. Muse VM / sandbox infrastructure

2 vCPUs, ~8 GB of RAM and ~100 GB of persistent logical storage per user. https://t.co/7rP5vDKnT7

2. Muse Spark inference

Model inference goes out through Meta's external inference infrastructure. https://t.co/e203XUp6jq
------

1/ Sandbox infrastructure

A. CPU
The first mistake is assuming that 100M DAU means 100M VMs are actively consuming compute at the same time.

Suppose the average Muse DAU has an agent actively working for two hours per day.

100M users * 2 hours / 24 hours = ~8M average simultaneous active VMs

Meta obviously cannot provision only for the daily average. Usage will be concentrated during waking hours and bursty.

Assume a 2.5x peak-to-average ratio:

8M * 2.5 = ~20M peak active VMs

Then add roughly 20% capacity headroom: ~25M provisioned live VMs. So the base assumption is effectively that Meta needs enough infrastructure to support roughly 25% of DAU being live simultaneously.

The next important distinction is between virtual CPU allocation and physical CPU demand. Agent sandboxes are particularly well suited to CPU oversubscription. They spend a lot of time waiting. During those periods, the VM may still be alive, but it is barely using CPU.

DeepSeek’s recently published DSec infrastructure provides a useful benchmark. Its production agent sandbox platform runs approximately 30,000 physical CPU cores and 250TB of DRAM across ~160 nodes, with peak concurrency above 380,000 sandboxes. https://t.co/PFlgc6nnUs DSec also demonstrates stable operation at around: 800 microVMs per node. With roughly 188 physical cores per node: 188 physical cores / 800 microVMs = ~0.23 physical cores per live VM.

DeepSeek is obviously the King of efficiency. The number for Muse might be at 0.3-0.75 physical cores per live VM, or assume 0.5 physical cores per live VM as the base case. That is equivalent to roughly two simultaneously live Muse VMs per physical CPU core.

Using the base assumptions: 25M live VMs * 0.5 physical cores per VM = 12.5M physical CPU cores.

On a 256-core CPU: 12.5M cores / 256 cores per CPU = ~50K CPUs; Or on a 192-core CPU that would be 65K CPUs.

At the current public pricing, that is ~$800M.

B. DRAM
CPU can be aggressively oversubscribed because a VM that is waiting may consume almost no CPU. Memory is harder to oversubscribe because a live VM still needs to retain its working state.

Muse exposes roughly 8GB of RAM to the user environment, but one observed instance was actually using only around 3GB at the time of measurement.

25M live VMs * 3GB = 75PB of physical DRAM, call it ~75-100PB of physical DRAM feels like a reasonable base range.

At the current public pricing, that is ~$2B.

C. Sandbox power
~0.1 GW for the entire Muse sandbox / VM layer at 100M DAU.

------

2/ Inference
Muse’s personal computer executes tools and stores state locally, but the actual model runs on separate inference infrastructure. Meta’s Muse architecture

Energy per inference event
Microsoft’s 2026 study estimates that optimized frontier-scale inference consumes a median of approximately: 0.31Wh per normal query

But a long reasoning query with roughly 15x the token count consumes approximately 13x as much energy, or around: 4Wh per long reasoning query

The study specifically highlights reasoning and agentic workloads as significantly more energy intensive.
https://t.co/z1YEsvVeMo

Sensitivity analysis on # reasoning-equivalent events per DAU per day

Suppose each active @Muse user generates the equivalent of 50 heavy inference events per day.

At 5Wh each:

100M users * 50 events/day * 5Wh = 25GWh/day

25GWh/day / 24 hours = ~1.0GW average power

So inference alone could require: ~1-2GW of average power

A 3-4GW Muse is entirely plausible. Maybe that’s why @Meta  is rumored to be adding 7-10GW of compute next year.

------
The popular framing around Muse is that giving every user 2 vCPUs and 8GB of RAM creates an enormous CPU requirement. But the naive calculation materially exaggerates the CPU requirement because it treats logical VM allocation as dedicated physical infrastructure.

The more interesting conclusion is: Consumer agents may be a meaningful new demand driver for CPUs and conventional DRAM, but inference remains the real compute bottleneck. And as agents do more work, run longer trajectories and increasingly spawn other agents, inference demand can scale much faster than the number of users itself.

Okay. I’ll take the bait.

I went to work for Peter in 2013 with opposite politics.

He sat me down right at the beginning. 

PETER: “I don’t want the (Thiel) Foundation to do good that the market can do. That is the job of the market. Likewise, I don’t want to do the good work that is seen as good. That work can be done by people richer, weaker and more needy of approval than we are. I want us to do only the work that is *deeply* good but somehow confused for being evil, because that is the work of the courageous and the strong. We strive to be both and that is where a small foundation can make the greatest positive difference. Go look for such good and let’s do that. But remember. Good has TWO different  antonyms. What is “bad work”? It could be seen as shoddy work. Or it could be seen as evil work. And we can’t do shoddy work. Why? Because evil that isn’t competent never gets to be evil. It’s just pathetic. So we have to be exceptionally competent at the good work which we do to make sure it is always confused for evil.”

I thought it totally logical. So that’s the argument. And that’s classic Peter. 

This is an old idea of his. And now you know.

The finger-pointing continues.

ICYMI, @kelpDAO’s dispute with @LayerZero_Core over April’s ~$292M bridge exploit is now heading to court.

For context, Kelp’s bridge relied on a single verifier run by LayerZero, so when attackers compromised the infrastructure feeding it data, there was no second independent check to stop the fake transfer.

LayerZero blamed Kelp’s setup, while Kelp said it had followed LayerZero’s defaults and guidance.

But LayerZero later acknowledged that allowing its verifier to operate alone for high-value transactions was a mistake.

So that’s the backdrop to this lawsuit: compromised infrastructure, disputed security guidance, and a $292M loss.

Who do you think was at fault here?

A medieval kingdom-themed multiplayer strategy game where players build kingdoms, recruit troops, and generate tokens every hour.

At the beginning, players choose a name and flag color, receive a plot of land + a Keep + 3 Pawns + 1,000 SW to start.

Upgrading the Keep unlocks buildings such as: Barracks, Armoury, Granary, Treasury, and Watchtower.

Soldiers must be “standing” to generate rewards. Pawn is the basic unit, and upgrading it to a Monk increases its output to 40x that of a Pawn while occupying the same slot.

Production continues even when players are offline.

There is a shared map + clan competition. The top 10 clans receive up to a +30% production bonus.

PVP is coming soon, along with 999 free-mint Genesis Banners NFTs.

The game has also integrated Rovyn DEX, allowing players to trade SW directly without leaving the game.

SW is the only currency in the game. Garrisoned troops mint $SW every hour.

Players use SW to upgrade buildings, recruit troops, and increase military ranks. The tokens spent are permanently burned.

Withdrawals from the Treasury carry a 5% fee. The first withdrawal requires a 12-hour waiting period, and the minimum withdrawal threshold was recently lowered to 20,000 tokens.

Seasons are limited, and there is a daily production cap.

So SW is both the reward and the cost of building. Tokens spent in the game are burned, creating a cycle where:

The more players invest into the game → the fewer tokens remain → the remaining tokens become more valuable.

The reasons behind the price increase should include the following:

Real user growth: More than 3,000 players within 56 hours. In the first 40 hours, there were already 2,350 players, 45,000 soldiers, and 53 clans.

Large amounts of tokens being consumed and burned in-game: 13% of the supply was already spent during the early stage.

Strong dev + playable product + deflationary mechanism: This combination has attracted capital and attention.

text:
很多人把 dontblink 当成又一个发射台叙事。
不是。

你套框架去打它，会打空。因为它不是靠一个叙事活着的，也不是靠一个 KOL、一个池子、一个上新节奏。

行业真正缺的不是下一个 24h 百倍。
是信任，和一个超过一周的时间尺度。
外面大部分 runner 一天可以归零，所以大家变成超短线，这很合理。
Don't hate the player hate the game.

但最大一拨人其实想做长期 holder。
他们被挤出 trenches 两年了，不是他们不想玩，是没人给他们一个能反复核对的发行层：锁仓是不是代码锁的、fee 进谁地址、登记表能不能被第三方认。

还有一类人更被忽视：朝九晚五，有家庭，不可能 24 小时盯盘。
他们平时买的是股票、ETF、退休账户那类“像真的东西”。
Robinhood Chain 把这类资产感接进来了，不等于你要变成 TradFi 传声筒。是把“能看懂的标的”和“链上仍能疯”叠在一起。

There is no one thing that can kill a real issuance layer.
能杀死一个资产的理由有一千个。dontblink 在做的，是让单一事故尽量杀不死整盘：池子、fee、登记、社区金库，分开放，能点开查。

关键不是完美设计。是平衡，而且每天改一点：

一、流动性要深到让上涨显得贵，但又不能深到完全没弹性。锁在合约里，不靠承诺。

二、要能靠 meme 速度分发，但又不能只剩纯 meme。股票计价、社区币、普通发射，可以并存，别做成单一品类赌场。

三、要有人 push，但不能变成一个人的号。原团队走了之后，费用进社区金库；方向得是 holder 也能认领的，不是创始人人格崇拜。

四、大盘砸的时候，整条生态不该一起死。接股票/RWA 感是减震，不是把加密周期红利冲掉。

五、站在增长快的链上，但不把分发全交给链本身。自己的站点、登记、fee 路径，要能独立讲清楚。

六、股票市场每天都有催化剂，但链上仍要有自己的叙事。只做映射会无聊，只做 meme 会脆。

七、长期目标可以慢，战术必须每天有。今天修发射检查，明天清 fee 领取路径，这才像在 ship，不像在开会。

八、要吃得到注意力行情，但不能靠overhype续命。数字用公开快照，别用口号。

九、可以重点推一条主线，比如社区币 / `$BLINK`，但不能 king-make 到其他资产全变 beta。hands-on launcher 翻车套路我见过太多次。

十、要压掉生态内纯 PVP 吸血，但保留不同资产、不同打法的竞争。健康竞争可以，互挖墙脚当商业模式不行。

这看起来像五维棋。
其实就四件事：活下来，跑得快，小步迭代，每天对着更大目标挪一点。

Fomo is the network.
Blink can become the issuance layer.

证伪你们自己做：
站上能核对登记发射和累计成交；treasury 有 memo；claimFees 是开放调用；流动性锁在合约里。这些任何一条对不上，上面整篇作废。

some thoughts for the weekend. 

So many people fail to realize there is no framework they can apply to LONG. There is no one central point of failure. There is no "one thing"  that can kill LONG because it’s driven by an iterative approach aimed at producing assets that are unique enough to never be fully priced in. The meta itself is a LONG term game.

The biggest issue in the space is a lack of trust and a longer term horizon (even a week), and it makes sense when almost every runner outside of LONG can go to 0 within a day. Don't hate the player hate the game.

We think the biggest category of people in crypto(or at least pattern) want to be long term holders, they also have the biggest potential to change the space. The issue, no one provides a systemic platform with high quality assets and many of them are completely sidelined from most of the activity the trenches had for the past two years.

Globally speaking, we also think the average Joe willing to trade/invest is not a hyper gambler or a meta rotational trader they work 9-5 might have a family and can't just watch the charts 24/7, they mostly allocate into “real” things like 401ks, ETF shares, and HOLDing some stocks and we want to prepare 

There are 1000 different things that can kill an asset. Every single thing we did with LONG is designed to mitigate these and make sure a top LONG pair won’t die because of a one bad thing that took place. 

The key is balance! There is no perfect setup. It’s iterative:

1. Deep liquidity that makes every pump well deserved while retaining liq for a LONG-term game, but still enables 100x returns.

2. Memetic assets that can drive distribution very fast, but are not just pure memes.

3. Having incredible impact from one dev/team pushing, but balancing that with strong community members who own the vision as well.

4. Making sure that when majors are nuking, it won’t kill the eco by connecting LONG assets to RWAs, but not to the point of losing the benefits of crypto cycles.

5. Aligning with the fastest growing chain we've seen for the past years but also drive our own dist.

6. Having an infinite number of catalysts coming from the stock market, but again, not to the point where there are no crypto narratives baked into it.

7. Being very focused on long-term targets that will take time to achieve, but playing a tactical game every day.

8. Retaining value from extreme hype and attention driven trading, but never overhype.

9. Pushing support to a core pillar like AI as a case study, but not to the point where all other assets are beta(also not king making assets and eventually top them like every "hands-on" launcher failed with in the past) 

10. Killing PVP from the inside with all sorts of mechs, but enabling healthy competition between different assets and approaches within the eco.

And the list goes on and on.

It might feel like 5D chess, but it’s really a simple playbook of surviving, moving really fast, iterating gradually, and making progress every day towards the bigger vision.

LONG.

text:
DAY 6586｜初めてのETHGlobal、本戦スタート

朝は亀戸を出て北千住へ。新店舗の工事進捗確認。

現地に着いて、いつもの番号でキーボックスを開けようとするも、まったく開かない。

鍵が中で引っかかってる？
番号が一桁ズレた？
誰かが番号を変えた？

不動産歴も長いので、今まで経験した「開かないパターン」を全部試したけどダメ。

工事関係者のLINEに連絡すると、

「そのキーボックスじゃないです」

え？

確認すると、本物は2階の踊り場に移動していた。

俺が必死に開けようとしていたのは、1階テナントのキーボックス（笑）

裏口で必死にキーボックスをガチャガチャしていたので、相当怪しいおじさんだったと思う。

無事に正しい鍵を発見し、店内へ。工事もほぼ完成していて一安心。

これはキーボックスにも名前を書いておいた方がいいな。

その後、日本橋へ。

業者との工事調整や、動き始めた「空き家再生×インバウンド宿」プロジェクトの候補物件探し。

そして今日一番大事なのが、夜から始まるETHGlobal Tokyoの準備。

過去の反省から、ハッカソンが始まってからアカウントを作ったり環境構築したりしていたら遅い。

必要なIDやアカウントなど、できる準備は先に全部済ませる。

今回は0回戦敗退だけはしない（笑）

17時、虎ノ門へ。

会場に着いてまず建物のすごさに圧倒される。

住居用エントランスなんて「資本主義の極み」みたいな世界。

受付も基本英語。

片言のパッション英語で受付を済ませ、Tシャツ、水筒、USB-Cケーブルなどを受け取って会場へ。

今回のハッカソンは3日間。

虎ノ門ヒルズの広いフロアを使い、ビルドスペース、ワークショップ会場、スポンサー企業のブース、さらに男女別の仮眠スペースまである。

そして食事、夜食、朝食、昼食、飲み物、お菓子、果物まで用意されている。

完全に3日間ハックするための環境。

まず今回使おうと思っているWorldのワークショップへ。

当然、全部英語。

そこでスマホの翻訳アプリを立ち上げ、音声をリアルタイム翻訳。それをイヤホンで聞くという力技で参加。

内容は理解できた。

20時から開会式。

それ以前にコードを書いてはいけないというルールなので、それまでは食事をしたり仕事のLINEを返したりして待機。

すると以前のハッカソンで会った人から声をかけてもらった。

ウォレットや暗号資産取引所の立ち上げ経験もあるエンジニアで、海外の同じハッカソンで受賞経験もあるらしい。

最近こういう場所に行くと、少しずつ知っている顔が増えてきた。

ようやく自分もこの界隈に入り始めた感じがして、ちょっと嬉しい。

開会式では最前列へ。

参加者は600人以上。

それでも経験者からすると、以前よりWeb3界隈は落ち着いているらしい。

自分は逆にAIから入って、今Web3に来た側。

だから全部が新しい。

開会式終了。

ここから正式にハック開始。

今回作るのは、

「空き家再生×インバウンド宿×本人確認×ブロックチェーン」

の仕組み。

宿泊者がパスポートなどで本人確認。

認証された本人にNFTの「鍵」を発行し、その鍵をウォレットに持たせる。

イメージとしては飛行機の搭乗券。

自分のウォレットに入ったデジタルの鍵を使って、宿泊施設へ入室する。

最初に「鍵をNFTにした方がいい」と言われた時は意味がよく分からなかった。

でも実際に作り始めると、

「ああ、こういうことか」

と少しずつWeb3の考え方がつながってきた。

まずWorldを使った本人認証を実装。

自分の認証までは成功。

次に「宿泊者が友人を招待する」機能をテストすると問題発生。

自分と友人の識別IDが同じになってしまう。

Worldの担当者ブースへ直行。

英語で説明するが、細かい技術の話になるとなかなか伝わらない。

そこでClaude Codeに状況を整理させ、英語の説明ページをその場で作成。

それを担当者に見せたら、一発で伝わった。

AIにコードを書かせながら、AIに英語も説明させて、人間同士でデバッグする。

すごい時代だなと思う。

結局、こちらの実装ミスとは断定できず、World側でも調査してもらうことになった。

待っている間に、パスポート以外の本人確認もテスト。

マイナンバーカードを使った認証も試して、こちらは問題なく動いた。

初日の目標だった本人認証部分は、とりあえず形になった。

今日はここまで。

そのまま会場で仮眠してもよかったけど、一度帰宅することに。

帰りにいつもの外国人が集まる店へ寄って、ワインを一杯だけ。

朝は北千住で他人のキーボックスを必死に開け、

夜は虎ノ門でデジタルの鍵を作っていた。

考えてみると、今日はずっと「鍵」と格闘していた1日だった（笑）

明日もハックは続く。

6600 DAYS

Spent a bit of time this morning looking into this

Based on this initial examination, I believe at least 1 relay solver may be leaking private intent data to sandwichers

Looking at the RH sandwich attacks conducted by these bots(*), every single sandwich contained at least 1 victim from Relay

One interesting thing to note about this is that often the swaps have multiple pools they can route through and Relay solvers do a primitive (**) form of onchain routing where they swap multiple candidate routes, reverting each one, and then selecting the best one to run. So that means the attackers have to perturb the pool just enough that they can profit but not so much that the solver routes through another pool

(*) Subset of bots where 100% of sandwiches have >=1 Relay victim (search period:  last 6 days)

author: imsongshu
quoted_text:
关于 dontblink 如何看待项目发射与扶持，我们想说几句。

随着 dontblink 不断成长，有一件事越来越重要：

不是每一个项目，都应该获得同等程度的扶持。

发射台不应该替一个还没有建立基础的项目去制造势能。

更合理的方式，是放大那些已经证明自己值得被更多人看见的项目。

────────────

项目负责打好基础，dontblink 负责放大势能。

在一切开始之前，我们首先看的是：

清晰的叙事。
健康的流动性。
真实的社区参与。
健康的链上结构。
持续的执行能力。
dontblink 可以放大势能。
但前提是，这个势能本身已经存在。
────────────
FDV 是阶段参考，不是自动解锁。

20K、50K、100K、200K、500K、1M 以及更高，都只是有意义的阶段节点。

但数字本身，不能说明一个项目是否健康。

两个 FDV 完全相同的项目，可能有完全不同的状态。

一个项目可能拥有更分散的持币结构、持续增长的流动性和活跃社区。

另一个项目，可能高度依赖少数几个钱包。

所以每一个阶段，我们仍然会综合判断：

流动性、持币分布、叙事质量、链上健康度和持续执行能力。

────────────

扶持力度，应该随着项目不断证明自己而增加。

当一个项目持续证明自己，dontblink 才会逐步开放更多网络资源。

最开始，可能只是官方层面的认可和曝光。

随着项目继续成长，支持可以进一步扩展到社区分发、生态资源、战略支持，以及更高阶段的交易所引荐。

逻辑很简单：

项目越强，dontblink 就越有理由提供更深度的支持。

────────────

双向共建同样重要。

有些项目不只是希望获得 dontblink 的曝光。

他们更希望成为生态的一部分。

如果项目愿意主动支持 dontblink Holder 社区，并持续为生态创造价值，就有机会获得更深度的 Community Support。

真正长期的合作，应该是双方都在为彼此创造价值。

────────────

dontblink 不希望成为短线项目的退出流动性。

这一点很重要。

dontblink 社区确实能够带来可观的关注度、参与度和真实买入。

但这些资源，不应该代替项目方本身的责任。

项目方仍然需要有自己的：

社区、流动性、分发能力和长期运营计划。

如果一个项目的所有势能，都依赖平台单方面推动，那么这种关系既不健康，也无法长期持续。

真实协同 > 单方面扶持。

────────────

dontblink 长期想做的，不是制造噪音，而是建立分发能力。

更多 Launch，本身不是终点。

真正重要的是项目发射之后发生什么。

社区能不能继续增长？
流动性能不能继续加深？
Holder 能不能留下来？
项目能不能突破第一阶段的上限，进入更大的市场？

这才是 dontblink 真正想发挥价值的地方。

我们不只想成为一个“发币的地方”。

我们想成为一张帮助优秀项目持续向上走的网络。

Launch → Community → Liquidity → Distribution → Ecosystem → Larger Markets
────────────
随着 dontblink 影响力不断增加，
我们对优秀项目能够提供的扶持力度，也会持续扩大。

我们还在早期。

但方向已经非常清楚。

打好基础。
建立真实势能。
dontblink 放大那些真正值得成长的项目。

don’t blink. 👀

text:
隐私技术都可以放在比特币了

最近一个密码学的研究团队，
发布了一篇论文名为，Shielded Bitcoin
他们提出的论述是，不改变比特币共识规则，
不进行软分叉，也不建立一条新的隐私链，
就可以让 $BTC 实现类似 $ZEC 的隐私转账。

这种屏蔽比特币不用改变比特币本身，而是在 Bitcoin L1 叠加一个隐私层，数据依然会保存在 L1 ，只是数据会被隐藏起来，外界不会看到转去哪里，转了多少。

听起来有点像 Zcash 。
没错，团队确实借鉴了 Zcash 的思路。

这对 $ZEC 来说可不是什么好事，
虽然它的技术得到认可，但如果未来比特币都能实现隐私转账，
那么它的定位就有点小尴尬了

不过这一切都还是纸上谈兵，
Shielded Bitcoin 只是一套研究方案
也还没解决实际的落地和应用。

到目前还没有克服要如何进入和退出隐私层，
团队表示第二篇论文会提出解决方案。

这个论文后我更相信隐私这个赛道会是下一个风口，
现在连比特币隐私都出来了。

不过， $ZEC 的技术可真牛逼，
牛逼到以后可能最大的对手就是比特币。

text:
The most interesting metric here: day-60 leaders still produced a median 15.9x gain after already surviving two separate 50% drawdowns.

Deep pullbacks reset the funding rates and shift supply from fast rotators to long-term holders who build the next floor.

So when you track genuine cultural leaders on Solana or Robinhood Chain, drawdowns are normal market structure. The real expansion phase often starts right after crash number two.
author: zerqfer
quoted_text:
Last cycle's biggest memes all looked dead at two months old.

By day 60, PEPE, WIF, BONK, FARTCOIN and the rest had each already come back from two or three drawdowns of 50% or more. Today's leaders on Robinhood Chain and Solana are on the same track.

Look at the blue box in the bottom left. The dashed orange icons are last cycle's winners at two months old, the blue ones are today's leaders. They sit right alongside each other.

What came next is the part most people seem to forget during these drawdowns. From day 60 to their top, the winners grew a median of 15.9x, and they had a median of 4 more drawdowns along the way. Every single one went through at least one more 50% drop before it topped and nobody got the 15.9x without sitting through the drops.

Worth mentioning: This only includes coins that went on to win, so it's what winning looked like, not how often it happens. We'll be tracking these leaders daily.

text:
proof of reserves gets way harder once part of the reserve leaves the chain.

you can verify a wallet in seconds.

but what happens when the hedge is sitting inside Binance?

this is one of the better @primus_labs use cases imo.

Unitas uses Primus + Brevis for $USDu reserve verification across both onchain positions and the CEX side of its delta-neutral strategy.

Primus zkTLS handles the important part:

→ proves the exchange data came from the real source  
→ keeps API keys and raw account data private  
→ turns that offchain information into verifiable input

then Brevis computes the final reserve proof.

so instead of:

“trust us, the hedge is there”

you can actually verify the data without making the entire trading account public.

this is where privacy + verification starts making a lot more sense for onchain finance.

text:
很难有人真正站在自己的利益之外，客观评价一个系统。

赚到钱的人吹，亏了钱的人骂。

看似在讨论制度、国家、社会，很多时候其实只是在表达：

“这个系统对我有利，还是对我不利。”

仓位决定脑袋。

而且“仓位”不只是股票。

你的职业、收入、房产、地域、阶层、身份，甚至你的出生，本身都是仓位。

纸都有两面。

很多人最大的问题，不是看错，而是永远只能看到对自己有利的那一面。

没有全局视角，也没有对手盘思维。

所以才会产生趋势。

因为每一个个体，都在寻找自己的局部最优解。

但无数个局部最优叠加起来，未必是全局最优。

这也是我为什么越来越期待AI治理。

不是因为AI天然正确，而是因为人类天然站在自己的位置上看世界。

而真正高级的AI，或许可以做一件人类很难做到的事：

同时站在所有人的位置上，看见每个人看不见的那一面。

从“仓位决定脑袋”，走向“全局决定局部”。

这可能才是AI治理真正值得期待的地方。
author: hazenlee
quoted_text:
大锅红利

一个系统的运行，即使再完美，也逃离不开几点：

1.系统不会让所有人满意，产生让所有人觉得公平的结果；
2.系统没有外部输血，那么内部有人吃亏，就一定有人受益；
3.系统再完美可控，依旧有BUG。

所以，这个系统好/不好，取决于你在系统里的生态位、怎么利用系统。不然你就算跑到火星，也是吃外星人脚皮的。

在中国这个系统里，你怎么享受红利呢？

1.想办法成为分蛋糕的群体：比如几年前，各路毕业即带编的院校并不难考，出来基本上能有一个稳定、收入不错的工作，享受老白杏爱的供养。知乎上看到一个思路：

前几年考中国人民公安大学、一路读到硕，毕业就能进一些地方的阿sir院校当老师：收入比普通公务员高、工作轻松不用有基层阿sir的压力、有寒暑假。这个系统比事业编、国央企更稳定，极端情况下系统依旧需要保利机关。

然后收入拿出来定投纳指。相当于中美世界上最强大的两个国家给你打工，绝对稳定、绝对反脆弱，横竖都是赚横竖都不亏。

2.拥有地理套利的能力：

比如出海赚美刀、能赚一线的收入在二线生活，二线城市的生活配置除了教育、顶尖医疗部分文体活动外其实和一线没太大差别，只要有万象城、山姆盒马、好气候好景色，就足矣满足90%以上的高品质生活需求。但是生活成本极低。

在资本回报高的地方赚钱，在资本回报低的地方享受廉价的商品和人力服务。

很多人抱怨国内卷、收入低、压力大，但是对我而言，中国目前是最完美的系统：

1.公共设施和服务价格低廉：坐个地铁3.4块、找华西毕业的博士医生咨询病情挂号费10块、开电车一个月电费30块；

2.私人商品和服务价格低廉：想吃外卖，花5块配送费半小时内就能满足食欲、理个发3.40块、出门吃饭口味好环境好的馆子不到100就能吃饱，在国外只能吃个冰激凌、叫保洁上门3小时100多给屋里收拾干净、旅游住亚朵300块非旺季五星级7.800，在国外只能住招待所。你过得比古代地主都舒服。

3.不打工，实际税率很低。a股拿着好公司长期持有，分红不缴税。

4.不是企业家，无需承担社会责任，不在体制内，没有乱七八糟规矩束缚，一身轻松。一年12个月，6个月自驾旅游6个月躺平敲键盘骂傻篮子和女拳。

每天饮食健康 认真锻炼 规律作息 干点自己喜欢的事，轻松开心活。阿马估计自己会很长寿，国内社会对老人也很好，老了继续享受红利￼

我爱你，中国！🇨🇳🇨🇳

无论是之前 Bybit/KelpDAO，还是前天 Bitget 被盗的赃款，全都在这过...

安全研究员 Taylor Monahan 去年接受 CoinDesk 采访时就曾表达过：THORChain 出现之前，ETH 换成 BTC 几乎一定会被冻。

黑客但凡走 CEX 或第三方桥，都很容易被冻。当时 KelpDAO 被盗时，Arbitrum 就冻住了约 7100 万美元的 ETH。

text:
I thought it was worth going over some of the main points from this article.

It was a good read, and this is what I took from it ↓

1️⃣ Your income is part of your risk management

A regular income covers expenses and gives you fresh capital. You don't have to force trades, sell at a bad time, or depend on one position paying the bills.

The market doesn't work around your expenses.

2️⃣ Liquidity matters more than market cap

Market cap shows price × supply. It doesn't show how much you can sell near that price.

Check order-book depth, volume, circulating supply, upcoming unlocks, and where the token trades.

Public tokens offer more control than locked private deals, but only when enough liquidity exists to enter and exit properly.

3️⃣ Set your DCA rules before buying

Choose a max allocation and specific review points before building the position.

At each review, check product usage, revenue, token demand, competition, supply growth, and team execution.

DCA spreads out an entry, so it shouldn't turn into unlimited buying while the thesis gets weaker.

4️⃣ Large selloffs often have a mechanical side

Liquidations, thin order books, and forced selling can push a token far below the level suggested by the news.

That doesn't automatically make it cheap, however, it does mean that the price is reflecting market structure, not just fundamentals.

Look at liquidation data, open interest, order-book depth, onchain flows, and spot selling to see whether holders are leaving or leveraged traders are being forced out.

5️⃣ Use more than one exit trigger

Price is only one reason to reduce a position.

Portfolio weight, valuation, token unlocks, slowing adoption, and stronger competition can matter just as much.

Selling in stages makes it easier if you recover the initial capital, reduce exposure as the position grows, and keep a smaller amount for long-term.

6️⃣ More trading doesn’t always mean more progress

Jumping between narratives usually leads to extra fees, weaker entries, and decisions driven by FOMO.

Start journaling your trades. Write down why you entered, how you were feeling, what could prove the idea wrong, and what would make you sell.

Over time, you’ll start noticing patterns in your own behaviour. You’ll see which decisions came from a solid process and which ones came from fear, greed, or impatience.

Overall, surviving a bull market comes down to discipline. Protect your capital, understand what you own, and have a plan before emotions take over.

We have confirmed that the so-called GIWA Mainnet we previously identified was in fact a fake chain set up by scammers.

The fake network used the correct GIWA Chain ID (9134), which made it appear legitimate during our initial verification. We have also identified specific suspicious messages and individuals in the related community that may be connected to this incident.

Unfortunately, significant losses have already occurred through the fraudulent bridge.

We are taking immediate action:

• We are contacting professional security teams to conduct further on-chain tracing and investigate the addresses, transactions, and flow of funds involved.

• We are preserving all relevant evidence, including chat records, RPC information, bridge addresses, and on-chain transactions.

• We are preparing to use funds from our treasury to compensate affected users. The eligibility criteria, loss verification process, compensation scope, and detailed plan will be announced after the investigation and verification process is completed.

Until further notice, DO NOT use any unofficial GIWA Mainnet RPC, bridge, or contract, and DO NOT send funds to any related addresses.

We sincerely apologize to everyone affected by this incident.

text:
i've played golf since i was 4

took almost 10 years off… 
came back this year

starting to understand why so many successful entrepreneurs love the sport

there’s so much that translates over to business

4 things it keeps teaching me:

1. you'll miss even after 10,000 reps
i’ve probably hit 10s of thousands of shots in my life, still get crazy misses

getting better doesn't mean you stop making mistakes, it just means you make them less often

2. every shot is a new one
75-90 a round, and before each one you're factoring in distance, wind, slope, turf, and the ball's lie. So no two rounds are ever the same, even on the same course

in business; markets, timing, users… they all keep changing. So what worked last time isn't guaranteed to work again. You need to reanalyze your decisions all the time

3. every shot matters the same
a 30cm putt is one stroke, just as ur longest drives

drives usually get the attention, but ur short game is what decides ur score

a big new fancy launch might get a lot of your focus, but it's the small stuff done well, every single day, that decides the long term outcome of your business

4.the shot that counts is the next one
never let a miss bring you down, figure out why it happened, what to do differently next time, then let it go

carry it with you, and one bad shot turns into two, three… then a whole round

both on the course and in business, what matters is what you do after your fuckups

bc the shot that rlly counts is always the next one

text:
我是一个Alpha Hunter，平时挂了很多监控，监控新链、新协议的启动，op L2 giwa链chain id之前在GitHub pr过，这条链也是大家一直在监控的一条热门的链。

今天凌晨有一个dev部署了一个同chain id的giwa，链上进来了大概2m资金，dyorswap同步接入并且在他们的tg群宣发平台启动。因为我之前玩arc、robinhood、blast、unichain、wld chain、plasma等等这些新链，都是差不多的进入路径，所以在验证了chain id没问题之后就想跨链进来拿一些早期进入机会。

之后，很多人都监控到了dyorswap加了新链，所以都在找进入新链的方法，同期就有很多地址在进入了，有朋友在微信群问我，我就把dyorswap发在tg群的新链信息发到了微信群。

我一直想在Web3闯出一番事业，所以在很多事情上操之过急，有的时候这能让我获得先发优势，有些时候这会让我摔个跟头。我这个推特是去年开始运营的，当时我的想法就是想成为链上alpha猎手，一边自己赚钱，一边力所能及的带朋友赚钱。

上上次robinhood链，我在很早发现了偷渡的方法，偷渡进去埋伏了几个币，并且带朋友埋伏了几个币，取得了一些早期收益。

上次arc链，我第一个扒到了gateway的跨链方法，所以早期发出来，很多人因为我的推文获得了早期进入机会。

我以为这种路径能复制下去，结果栽了跟头。

因为我技术的匮乏，没有预料到GIWA主网在GitHub已经提交了chain id pr的情况下，还能有个人开发者larp一条假链的情况存在，但之前的成功经历，让我路径依赖。出于想要获得推特流量的想法、出于渴望获得别人的认可，我在推特转发了这条假链的启动信息。

随后就是大家知道的情况。

实在对不起所有人，事情发生后我就陷入了深深的自责之中，我接受所有朋友对我的批评与谩骂，也看到了有朋友截图我在我的tg群里的话，虽然那些话是复制群友玩梗的话，但毕竟出自我口，我从来没有预料到我从当初籍籍无名到现在有一定的影响力，更应该谨言慎行这一点。

对不起大家。

另外，我尽我所能对诈骗链、诈骗桥的信息进行了一定的溯源，最初的资金来源指向币安 @binance  和GATE @Gate  的两笔提币，以及 @Changehero_io 的一笔跨链交易。希望这些信息能够帮到大家一些。信息我会整理到下一条线程，再次跟所有人诚挚的说一声抱歉，对不起！

text:
We are officially witnessing the biggest wave of infrastructure investment in modern US history.

Total investment in data centers and AI infrastructure is projected to average 3.63% of US GDP per year from 2025 to 2032, the highest proportion among major infrastructure buildouts since the 1800s.

The previous largest investment, railroad infrastructure, represented 2.24% of GDP per year in 1870-1890.

This was followed by highway investment that averaged 1.13% of GDP in 1956-1973, while telecommunications and fiber infrastructure averaged 1.10% in 1996-2003.

By comparison, electrification stood at just 0.50% of GDP in 1905-1925, while canal investment accounted for 0.66% in 1836-1841.

This comes as AI and data-center infrastructure investment is projected to total ~$10.3 trillion between 2025 and 2032.

The AI buildout is the largest infrastructure investment in modern US history.

text:
贝莱德这篇论文，把 AI × Crypto 最重要的一条钱路讲明白了：以后机器会自己花钱（都是知识）

AI Agent 真正跑起来以后，它每天都要买数据、调用 API、租 GPU、订软件，而且很多交易可能只有几美分，却要求 7×24 小时自动完成。

信用卡、ACH 这些支付系统本来是围绕“人”设计的，Agent 需要一套机器可以直接调用、即时结算、金额可以小到几分钱的金融系统。

贝莱德给出的答案就是稳定币 + 区块链。

2025 年过滤掉交易所内部转账、机器人等噪音后，稳定币交易量已经达到 11.2 万亿美元，2020—2025 年复合增速 80%，同期 ACH 只有约 8.5%。

更重要的是，Agent 通过 x402 买 API、用稳定币付款，每增加一次机器交易，都可能继续传导成区块空间、验证和结算需求，最后碰到 ETH 这类公链原生资产。

但我觉得贝莱德这篇最有意思的地方，其实是后半段：

算力可能会直接变成一种金融资产。

2025—2030 年 AI 基础设施累计资本开支可能超过 5 万亿美元，AWS、微软 Intelligent Cloud 和 Google Cloud 到 2030 年收入合计预计约 1.1 万亿美元。

到那时候，AI 推理预计会吃掉全球数据中心约 43% 的电力需求。

以后 GPU 算力使用权完全可能被标准化、代币化，做成可以交易、融资、抵押甚至对冲的资产，Agent 自己比价格、延迟和芯片型号，然后自动买算力、自动付款。

这条链一旦跑通，Crypto 面对的用户就不只是一群人在交易资产，而是海量 AI Agent 全天候买数据、买算力、做支付、做结算。

稳定币变成机器的现金，公链变成机器的结算层，Tokenized RWA 是机器可以调用的资产，算力甚至可能成为下一类链上商品。

贝莱德已经开始按这个框架重新看数字资产了。

text:
【从 CME、Silicon Data 到 0G ， Compute Finance 算力金融化的不同侧面，都在试图解决什么？】

最近浅浅看了一些关于算力金融化的研究，但比较多的还是集中在偏传统金融的领域。

恰好又看到了前两天 @0G_labs  的推文，在这方面做出了一些新的动作，并且还结合了自身代币的延期解锁‼️

接下来简单分享一下👇

（为了不让本文过于冗长，就不讲述太多大而全的前置信息了）

➠ 一、Compute Finance 的整体结构

为了便于理解，我们需要首先建立一个总体框架。

如果把 Compute Finance 的结构分成以下八层，那么目前一些相关方的尝试可以按照这样的形式来划分。如图。

（⚠️注意：我这里的框架是个非常初期和粗糙的版本，仅作为参考、方便理解）

▪️诸如 Silicon Data、CME 这样的机构正在尝试给算力建立价格体系和风险管理系统；

▪️而 0G 这样的 crypto 项目则在尝试给算力建立一种链上持有和使用方式。

————————————————

➠ 二、算力金融化的不同侧面

这里仅以我近期看得稍多一点的三个实体（ CME、Silicon Data、0G ）出发作为例子，这个框架下仍然有许多其他的公司/机构/项目待讨论。

1️⃣ Silicon Data 做的是算力的标准化和价格基础设施

它试图把分散、异质、不可直接比较的 GPU 租赁报价，转换成统一的 GPU-hour 基准价格，并进一步形成价格指数和远期曲线

2️⃣ CME 金融化的是算力价格

它的出发点是一个已经存在的商业问题：AI 公司、数据中心和 GPU 租赁商都要面对未来算力价格的不确定性，通过尝试把算力放进既有的大宗商品金融体系里，让算力价格变得可以被观察、预测和交易。

注：CME 原定于 10 月 5 日上线 H100 和 B200 租赁指数期货，但前几日 CFTC 把审查期延长到了 11 月 9 日（看来这些新玩意儿问世的时间又变得充满不确定性了🤔）

3️⃣ 0G 金融化的是算力使用权

它的出发点是：如果算力会成为 AI 经济最重要的生产资料，用户和 AI Agent 能不能像持有资本一样持有算力？

————————————————

➠ 三、0G 在算力金融化领域做出的尝试

0G 的尝试主要是通过 Ascend 和 Infinite AI 两个阶段完成

1️⃣ Ascend

Ascend 已于 9 月 24 日随 Compute Finance 公布而上线。用户质押 0G 获得 a0G；这使质押中的 0G 保留了一定的 DeFi 可组合性，并继续参与质押收益。

2️⃣ Infinite AI

计划于 9 月 29 日上线。

♻ 按照官方设计，用户可以锁定 a0G  → 铸造 iAI  → 质押 iAI  → 获得可用于 0G Private Computer 和 0G App 等支持服务的 AI compute credits

因为 0G 自身已经提供包括 0G Private Computer 在内的 AI 服务，并支持 100 多个模型，用户理论上可以在这个体系内完成从质押 0G、获得链上资产，到实际使用 AI 服务额度的闭环。甚至长期来看，AI Agent 也可能成为这类算力资产的持有者和使用者。

这样，算力在未来不再只是 AI 的成本项，而成为 AI 经济中的生产资料。

————————————————

当然这其中有非常多的不确定因素，所以目前阶段很多是早期的探索，但加密世界最不缺的就是探索精神以及无需许可下进行的快速发展与迭代

‼️另外值得注意的是，近期 0G 团队和早期投资者还主动选择了延期一年解锁，把占供应量 44% 的代币的首次解锁时间从 2026.10.22 推迟到了 2027.10.22

🫳
Let’s Stay Tuned
🫴

text:
Rufus-Air is a blueprint for building strong open LLMs with nothing but public data and accessible compute—no secret sauce, no new human labels, no in-house distillation. The team takes a 106B MoE base (GLM-4.5-Air-Base) and walks it through 8 post-training stages, from massive supervised fine-tuning (9M samples) to targeted RL for reasoning, coding, tool use, and alignment.

The gains are real: SFT alone beats the vendor’s official release on key instruction and math tasks. Then RL boosts Multi-Challenge by +24.7pp, LiveCodeBench by +7.3pp, Tau2-Retail by +9.8pp, and creative writing by +14.4pp—outperforming GLM-4.5-Air nearly everywhere, and going toe-to-toe with top open models like INTELLECT-3.

Every step is documented: learnability filtering, reward ordering by reliability, open infrastructure (FP8, router replay, Firecracker sandboxes), and orchestration with Ray. All reproducible, all open.

If you want to build or extend capable LLMs without a mega-lab budget, this is the playbook.

Get the full analysis here: https://t.co/WuNv0gIv6K

text:
What if NFT communities can turn memecoin speculation into a recurring acquisition budget?

Yes, we are talking about @UseNosh.

Different from other 'launchpads', Nosh targets an NFT collection. Trading generates creator fees, which accumulate until they can fund purchases near the collection’s lowest asking price. Multiple coins can contribute to a shared collection vault.

Nosh is live on @ponsdotfamily with 80% of collected creator fees funds purchases; 20% goes to Nosh’s treasury.

Purchased NFTs are raffled to holders with balance-weighted odds, or burned under the coin’s fixed policy. Holding the coin provides no guaranteed NFT or redemption right.

The live product connects several distinct systems:

Pons V2 → @Uniswap v4, on @RobinhoodCrypto Chain: launch, trading and fee generation. Seaport 1.6 executes local NFT purchases; OpenVRF/drand supplies raffle randomness. Docs

@Pumpfun → Nosh vaults, on @Solana: another source of creator fees. Native NFT purchases can execute through Tensor, with a locked 80% vault allocation. Live example

@zilkroad_ / @Zcash → the documented purchasing route for zkSNARKs NFTs. External purchases require an operator, announced withdrawals and recorded receipts. External route

The NFTs purchasing target so far:

▸ EVM → CryptoPunks, BAYC, Pudgy Penguins, Milady Maker, Doodles, Cool Cats and VeeFriends.

▸ Solana → Mad Lads, DeGods, SMB Gen2, Retardio Cousins, Claynosaurz and y00ts.

▸ HyperEVM → Hypurr.

▸ Zcash → zkSNARKs.

Personally, this is quite refreshing idea, Nosh creates a concrete link between memecoin activity and NFT demand. Its lasting advantage depends on sustained trading, reliable execution, and community loyalty.

So, are we gonna have another NFT season?

1. 中国AI模型非常强，尤其“单位算力产出的智能”全球领先；中国高端芯片和算力瓶颈可能在2–3年内明显缓解。

2.Grok目前仍落后于Anthropic最前沿模型，但xAI的差异化方向不是只做聊天和编程，而是利用Tesla、SpaceX数据打造“现实世界工程AI”。

3.Tesla的未来重点越来越明确：自动化和Optimus机器人，而不只是卖电动车。

4.Cybercab从一开始就是为完全无人驾驶设计，没有方向盘和踏板，Cybercab已在Texas商业运营，接下来将进入佛罗里达、内华达等州，预计到2027年年中左右进入加州。

5.Elon预测人形机器人会迎来爆发式增长：未来10年可能达到10亿台，之后规模会继续快速扩大。

6.机器人将承担制造、家务、养老、教育等大量工作，一个人，未来可能管理成百上千个数字Agent 和实体机器人。

7. AI+机器人最终可能让社会进入“Universal High Income”，劳动成本大幅下降，商品和服务趋向极度丰富。

8.Elon认为AI带来积极未来的概率约90%，但超级智能仍存在风险，中美应该建立AI安全合作机制。

9. AI竞争不只是芯片竞争，电力同样关键；中国庞大的发电能力是一个重要长期优势。

10.Starship最关键的目标是“完全、快速重复使用”，只有这样才能真正大幅降低进入太空的成本。

11.火星的意义一方面是给人类文明增加“保险”，另一方面是给人类一个值得期待的宏大目标。

12.Neuralink的长期目标之一，是解决人类和AI之间通信带宽过低的问题。

13.对年轻人的建议：不要只学 AI 或编程，而要尽可能接受广泛教育；未来真正稀缺的能力，是知道“应该让 AI 做什么”。

text:
🤡我说了很多小伙伴都不信，最好的保持精力的方式就是轻断食，让自己保持的适度的饥饿状态，但不是那种饥肠辘辘，尤其是我最近的体检指标远远的高于同龄者。

这也是为什么很多小伙伴现在都在打针的原因，就是为了让自己少吃点，起到减肥的作用，但我觉得轻断食的本质并不是为了减肥，而是减少疲劳，改善每天的精力状态。这方面也确实有一些人体研究支持。

2022年《JAMA内科学》发表过一项涉及90名肥胖成年人的随机对照试验，持续了14周。两组都接受控制热量的减重干预，其中一组把吃饭时间集中在早上7点到下午3点，另一组的进食时间跨度至少有12小时。

结果发现，前一组除了体重下降更多，问卷里的疲劳感和活力评分也有更明显的改善。也就是说，这项研究观察到的变化，确实包括“感觉没那么累、更有精神”。

而且从我个人的体感来看，起码是我个人吃饱了的时候就非常会容易晕碳，会出现非常想睡觉或者休息的情况，感觉有点“慵懒”，而不像在保持略微饥饿的时候那么精力旺盛。

text:
In January, Iran went dark. The internet was cut, independent reporting was suppressed and foreign journalists were kept out.

What happened next was recorded largely by the people who were there.

This Is Our Story brings together footage filmed across Iran with first-hand accounts from eyewitnesses, survivors and bereaved families. Much of this material reached the outside world only in fragments. The four-part series places those images back into sequence and, where possible, verifies when and where they were recorded.

The aim is simple: to preserve the evidence, give the footage its context, and create a fuller record of what happened.

With English subtitles throughout, the series is intended for audiences inside and outside Iran.

مستند «This Is Our Story» با زیرنویس انگلیسی منتشر می‌شود تا جهان صدای مردم ایران را بشنود و ببیند در دی‌ماه چه بر آنان گذشت؛ به‌ویژه صدای کسانی که برای ثبت و رساندن این تصاویر، جان و امنیت خود را به خطر انداختند. بدون شجاعت آنان، بسیاری از وقایع آن روزها هرگز دیده نمی‌شد.

بخش بزرگی از آنچه به جهان رسید، تصاویری پراکنده و اغلب بدون خط زمانی و زمینهٔ کافی بود. این مستند، تصاویر و روایت‌های دست‌اول را در یک روایت پیوسته کنار هم قرار می‌دهد تا مخاطبان غیرفارسی‌زبان نیز بتوانند روند وقایع، ابعاد سرکوب و آنچه مردم تجربه کردند را بهتر درک کنند.

زیرنویس انگلیسی برای این است که زبان، مانعی برای شنیدن این شهادت‌ها نباشد و تصاویری که با چنین هزینه‌ای ثبت و به بیرون از ایران فرستاده شدند، به مخاطبان بیشتری برسند.

quoted_text:
⚠️ Security Incident Notice

We have confirmed that the so-called GIWA Mainnet we previously identified was in fact a fake chain set up by scammers.

The fake network used the correct GIWA Chain ID (9134), which made it appear legitimate during our initial verification. We have also identified specific suspicious messages and individuals in the related community that may be connected to this incident.

Unfortunately, significant losses have already occurred through the fraudulent bridge.

We are taking immediate action:

• We are contacting professional security teams to conduct further on-chain tracing and investigate the addresses, transactions, and flow of funds involved.

• We are preserving all relevant evidence, including chat records, RPC information, bridge addresses, and on-chain transactions.

• We are preparing to use funds from our treasury to compensate affected users. The eligibility criteria, loss verification process, compensation scope, and detailed plan will be announced after the investigation and verification process is completed.

Until further notice, DO NOT use any unofficial GIWA Mainnet RPC, bridge, or contract, and DO NOT send funds to any related addresses.

We sincerely apologize to everyone affected by this incident.

Further updates will be published as soon as more information becomes available.

author: cfm_sol
quoted_text:
some thoughts for the weekend. 

So many people fail to realize there is no framework they can apply to LONG. There is no one central point of failure. There is no "one thing"  that can kill LONG because it’s driven by an iterative approach aimed at producing assets that are unique enough to never be fully priced in. The meta itself is a LONG term game.

The biggest issue in the space is a lack of trust and a longer term horizon (even a week), and it makes sense when almost every runner outside of LONG can go to 0 within a day. Don't hate the player hate the game.

We think the biggest category of people in crypto(or at least pattern) want to be long term holders, they also have the biggest potential to change the space. The issue, no one provides a systemic platform with high quality assets and many of them are completely sidelined from most of the activity the trenches had for the past two years.

Globally speaking, we also think the average Joe willing to trade/invest is not a hyper gambler or a meta rotational trader they work 9-5 might have a family and can't just watch the charts 24/7, they mostly allocate into “real” things like 401ks, ETF shares, and HOLDing some stocks and we want to prepare 

There are 1000 different things that can kill an asset. Every single thing we did with LONG is designed to mitigate these and make sure a top LONG pair won’t die because of a one bad thing that took place. 

The key is balance! There is no perfect setup. It’s iterative:

1. Deep liquidity that makes every pump well deserved while retaining liq for a LONG-term game, but still enables 100x returns.

2. Memetic assets that can drive distribution very fast, but are not just pure memes.

3. Having incredible impact from one dev/team pushing, but balancing that with strong community members who own the vision as well.

4. Making sure that when majors are nuking, it won’t kill the eco by connecting LONG assets to RWAs, but not to the point of losing the benefits of crypto cycles.

5. Aligning with the fastest growing chain we've seen for the past years but also drive our own dist.

6. Having an infinite number of catalysts coming from the stock market, but again, not to the point where there are no crypto narratives baked into it.

7. Being very focused on long-term targets that will take time to achieve, but playing a tactical game every day.

8. Retaining value from extreme hype and attention driven trading, but never overhype.

9. Pushing support to a core pillar like AI as a case study, but not to the point where all other assets are beta(also not king making assets and eventually top them like every "hands-on" launcher failed with in the past) 

10. Killing PVP from the inside with all sorts of mechs, but enabling healthy competition between different assets and approaches within the eco.

And the list goes on and on.

It might feel like 5D chess, but it’s really a simple playbook of surviving, moving really fast, iterating gradually, and making progress every day towards the bigger vision.

LONG.

text:
Peter Thiel 最近说了一句很不像 Peter Thiel 的话：

AI 可能养不出几个真正的垄断巨头，最后便宜的反而是消费者。

Thiel 过去最出名的一套商业理论，就是竞争是给失败者准备的，好公司要想办法逃离竞争，建立垄断。Google、Facebook 这些互联网公司，基本就是他心目中的标准答案。

结果到了 AI，他开始觉得这套剧本可能演不下去了。

《泰晤士报》报道，Thiel 判断 AI 时代产生的垄断公司可能比互联网时代更少，而且 AI 创造的相当一部分价值最终会流向消费者。

翻译一下，AI 当然可能创造天量价值，但这笔钱未必留在做 AI 的公司账上。

这个区别其实很要命。

现在大家给 OpenAI、Anthropic 这些公司估值，多少都藏着一个熟悉的互联网剧本：

模型越做越强，用户越积越多，最后赢家通吃，形成下一个 Google 级别的利润池。

但 AI 目前偏偏在往另一个方向跑。

模型能力差距不断被追，价格不断往下打，开源模型在后面追着放血。你这周刚把 benchmark 拉开，下个月别人追上来了；你刚准备靠能力领先涨价，隔壁又把 token 打成白菜。

AI 比互联网重要得多，AI 公司却未必有互联网巨头那么好赚钱。

技术革命成功了，消费者赢麻了，模型公司每天继续卷 benchmark。

Thiel 研究了一辈子怎么逃离竞争，到了 AI 这里一看，大家可能谁也逃不掉。

This is to my point about compression being inevitable as human knowledge is too small for what we are building. As well, humans are too redundant in their wants needs and questions. 

AI-generated content will clearly contain propagation errors just like human history of knowledge does. Only LLMs will iterate those propagation errors infinitely faster with less ability to self- correct, for want of understanding. 

This gets to Ballard’s test. LLMs cannot attain understanding (AGI) as understanding cannot exist unless reason first exists without language. A likely impossibility for a language model. 

Research on this is already focused on getting around this in some way. Though many also have not yet conceded the point.
author: michaeljburry
quoted_text:
ChatGPT has now a big problem.

Researchers at Oxford and Cambridge exposed a massive threat to large language models.”

They call it “model collapse."

Internet ecosystem is rapidly changing, and generative AI will soon contribute much of the text found online. This forces us to consider what happens to future iterations like gpt-n when they are trained on data scraped from the web that was already generated by an llm.

According to the research, indiscriminately using model-generated content in training causes "irreversible defects" in the resulting ai. the model loses the "tails of the original content distribution." in other words, it begins to forget the creative, fringe, and unique nuances of actual human writing, collapsing into a repetitive echo chamber.

This isn't just a chatgpt issue.. the researchers built theoretical intuition showing this collapse is ubiquitous across learned generative models, occurring in large language models as well as in variational autoencoders and gaussian mixture models.

Tech companies rely on scraping the internet for large-scale data to build smarter models. However, the paper warns that if we want to sustain the benefits of training on web data, model collapse must be taken seriously.

Ultimate takeaway? data collected from genuine human interactions is going to become increasingly valuable in a web filled with ai content.

Season 3 is expected in 2027.

AI can think. But who verifies that it is right?

Today, we trust AI models as black boxes.

We send a request → receive an answer → make a decision.

But in critical areas, trust alone is not enough.

Finance. Autonomous agents. Smart contracts. Medical systems.

We need AI where results are not only generated, but verifiable.

This is where the idea of verifiable AI becomes important.

Baranos introduces a new approach: creating a layer of trust between AI models and users by making AI computations verifiable.

My use case:

Verifiable AI agents for DeFi.

Today:

An AI agent analyzes the market
Makes a decision
Executes a transaction

But users still have to blindly trust the agent.

With Baranos:

The agent can provide evidence behind its computation
Decisions become transparent
Users can verify the process instead of only trusting the outcome

Who benefits?

> DeFi users
> Financial protocols
> Developers building autonomous AI agents

The future of AI is not only intelligence.
It is intelligence + proof.

There is some brutal honesty in this post

He’s right in that you can’t just go into a business, slap on some Claude licenses and drop a few agents and expect P&L to magically improve

author: KSimback
quoted_text:
Here’s why Greg is wrong, from someone who bought, grew, and sold one of these:

Nobody running of these is dumb, and the fact that they've survived is testament to the fact that they're smart.

To me, baked into this strategy is a sense of paternalism. Look at these dumb boomers. I can come in with absolutely zero industry experience and a Claude Code subscription and change this industry!!

The most pervasive dynamic within Main Street businesses is resource scarcity. 

Not enough time or money to do any of the million things that you plan to.

Awesome, so you want to do some big Claude Code thing? 

Cool, you're going to need to find time to do that between figuring out how to repair the trucks, fix your broken Google My Business listing, and not take a salary that month because of the reinvestment you're making with the hope that it will pay off.

Getting a CRM implemented correctly is hard enough!!

You need managers who enforce the process, employees who change their habits, and someone accountable when things break. 

Now try rebuilding delivery around AI WHILE KEEPING THE BUSINESS ALIVE AND SERVICING DEBT.

 You come in full of piss and vinegar and on day four your operations manager quits because she liked doing things the old way, and suddenly you’re covering her job instead of building agents. 

Greg acknowledges key-person risk, but it deserves far more weight in his economics. 

The people, process, and change management required to make even basic technology productive can consume years.

Innovation has to improve the performance of the whole business. 

Justin Roff-Marsh and I have discussed the sequence: identify the constraint, get more productive use from its existing capacity, then add capacity where necessary to increase throughput. 

Said another way ---If an accounting firm’s bottleneck is senior review, generating drafts ten times faster may just create a bigger queue. 

You have to show how AI frees the reviewer, change the workflow so that capacity gets used, and then upgrade whatever limits further growth. 

Technological innovation must drive global maxima, not local maxima.

Even real savings elsewhere need to be converted into lower expenses (which is only weak replacement) or redeployed against the constraint. 

A list of automated tasks tells me very little about how much more profitable work the firm can complete.

Now put a large, expensive acquisition loan underneath that transition. 

In the SBA buying range, debt payments compete with the money you need for implementation, training, replacement hires, and additional capacity. 

Saving people time doesn’t automatically remove their salaries. 

Your plan is to do what? Have Betty train you in the first three weeks to replace her, and then you're gonna fire her. Let me know how that goes for you with a big ass loan due every month.

More than likely you're going to end up keeping Betty and adding a bunch of AI expenses, which are going to reduce all of your fancy pre-acquisition projections.

You can spend months paying for the existing payroll, new software, and human review before realizing any savings....  If at all.

And cutting a support role can make your scarce, expensive specialists less productive if they inherit its work. 

Ultimately a playbook like the below is achievable but requires an enormous amount of experience, judgment, skill, etc. 

And the idea that a corporate refugee is going to parachute in out of their W2 with a couple agents and transform a business model fundamentally feels like something that someone who's never tried to do it before in a real business would say.

I'm happy to have this debate with anybody who'd like to have it. I've both owned these businesses and built agents in an enormous number of these categories referenced.

quoted_text:
A humble attempt to est. the infra required to serve 100M DAU @Muse 

Rough conclusion is:

1 GW of power to serve 100M DAU in the base case, of which only ~0.1 GW comes from the CPU/VM layer. Depending on the # of reasoning-equivalent model calls one Muse DAU generates per day, 3-4GW is entirely plausible. Maybe that’s why @Meta  is rumored to be adding 7-10GW of compute next year.

The sandbox layer = sub $1B of CPU content and ~$2B of DRAM content, which is much smaller than many expected.

Lot of moving assumptions. Welcome all feedbacks/ pushbacks.

------
Two very different pieces of infrastructure behind Muse.

1. Muse VM / sandbox infrastructure

2 vCPUs, ~8 GB of RAM and ~100 GB of persistent logical storage per user. https://t.co/7rP5vDKnT7

2. Muse Spark inference

Model inference goes out through Meta's external inference infrastructure. https://t.co/e203XUp6jq
------

1/ Sandbox infrastructure

A. CPU
The first mistake is assuming that 100M DAU means 100M VMs are actively consuming compute at the same time.

Suppose the average Muse DAU has an agent actively working for two hours per day.

100M users * 2 hours / 24 hours = ~8M average simultaneous active VMs

Meta obviously cannot provision only for the daily average. Usage will be concentrated during waking hours and bursty.

Assume a 2.5x peak-to-average ratio:

8M * 2.5 = ~20M peak active VMs

Then add roughly 20% capacity headroom: ~25M provisioned live VMs. So the base assumption is effectively that Meta needs enough infrastructure to support roughly 25% of DAU being live simultaneously.

The next important distinction is between virtual CPU allocation and physical CPU demand. Agent sandboxes are particularly well suited to CPU oversubscription. They spend a lot of time waiting. During those periods, the VM may still be alive, but it is barely using CPU.

DeepSeek’s recently published DSec infrastructure provides a useful benchmark. Its production agent sandbox platform runs approximately 30,000 physical CPU cores and 250TB of DRAM across ~160 nodes, with peak concurrency above 380,000 sandboxes. https://t.co/PFlgc6nnUs DSec also demonstrates stable operation at around: 800 microVMs per node. With roughly 188 physical cores per node: 188 physical cores / 800 microVMs = ~0.23 physical cores per live VM.

DeepSeek is obviously the King of efficiency. The number for Muse might be at 0.3-0.75 physical cores per live VM, or assume 0.5 physical cores per live VM as the base case. That is equivalent to roughly two simultaneously live Muse VMs per physical CPU core.

Using the base assumptions: 25M live VMs * 0.5 physical cores per VM = 12.5M physical CPU cores.

On a 256-core CPU: 12.5M cores / 256 cores per CPU = ~50K CPUs; Or on a 192-core CPU that would be 65K CPUs.

At the current public pricing, that is ~$800M.

B. DRAM
CPU can be aggressively oversubscribed because a VM that is waiting may consume almost no CPU. Memory is harder to oversubscribe because a live VM still needs to retain its working state.

Muse exposes roughly 8GB of RAM to the user environment, but one observed instance was actually using only around 3GB at the time of measurement.

25M live VMs * 3GB = 75PB of physical DRAM, call it ~75-100PB of physical DRAM feels like a reasonable base range.

At the current public pricing, that is ~$2B.

C. Sandbox power
~0.1 GW for the entire Muse sandbox / VM layer at 100M DAU.

------

2/ Inference
Muse’s personal computer executes tools and stores state locally, but the actual model runs on separate inference infrastructure. Meta’s Muse architecture

Energy per inference event
Microsoft’s 2026 study estimates that optimized frontier-scale inference consumes a median of approximately: 0.31Wh per normal query

But a long reasoning query with roughly 15x the token count consumes approximately 13x as much energy, or around: 4Wh per long reasoning query

The study specifically highlights reasoning and agentic workloads as significantly more energy intensive.
https://t.co/z1YEsvVeMo

Sensitivity analysis on # reasoning-equivalent events per DAU per day

Suppose each active @Muse user generates the equivalent of 50 heavy inference events per day.

At 5Wh each:

100M users * 50 events/day * 5Wh = 25GWh/day

25GWh/day / 24 hours = ~1.0GW average power

So inference alone could require: ~1-2GW of average power

A 3-4GW Muse is entirely plausible. Maybe that’s why @Meta  is rumored to be adding 7-10GW of compute next year.

------
The popular framing around Muse is that giving every user 2 vCPUs and 8GB of RAM creates an enormous CPU requirement. But the naive calculation materially exaggerates the CPU requirement because it treats logical VM allocation as dedicated physical infrastructure.

The more interesting conclusion is: Consumer agents may be a meaningful new demand driver for CPUs and conventional DRAM, but inference remains the real compute bottleneck. And as agents do more work, run longer trajectories and increasingly spawn other agents, inference demand can scale much faster than the number of users itself.

text:
This accident disclosure just revealed what everyone in the industry already knows: the curator business model doesn’t work without someone continuously paying for integrations and LP deals.

DeFi was supposed to cut out the middleman. Yet with this model, you can end up stacking as many as five layers of fees: integrator fees, curator fees (sometimes charged both onchain and offchain as “consulting” fees to asset issuers), LP fees, and middleware fees (we do not expect it will be forever free, right?).

Unlike Web2, DeFi enables extreme composability. Eg if you are not on Amazon, you can not sell your product. But in DeFi, you can be fully integrated everywhere via smart contracts. In this environment, owning the underlying protocol and its economics can be far more valuable than the potential benefits of broader distribution deals.
author: megabyte0x
quoted_text:
A lot of people reached out asking about paid integrations, how protocols can even compete, and what the growth perspectives are for Fluid in this case. Here are some thoughts:  Paying for integrations and exclusivity is simply part of growth strategy and business development. That's completely normal. A lot of people just do not know about this and think that eg Morpho is getting all integrations by default.   Morpho has a very strong backing and an excellent BD team, but they won't be able to pay for every integration forever. There is also the question of alignment between partners.

Eg the Coinbase deal reportedly cost ~7x less than the Robinhood deal, yet Coinbase accounts for more than 60% of Morpho's TVL and has been a major contributor to $morpho becoming the highest-valued lending protocol. This high valuation helped to finance the deal with Robinhood, which is a direct competitor to Coinbase. CB is well known for their negotiating skills, so it'll be interesting to see what happens when they revisit that relationship.

I also agree with what @euler_mab said about tokens. A new token can open many doors. Like Euler, we chose not to launch with a new token and instead continued with the token from the previous protocol from 2021. That decision came with limitations, but when one opportunity closes, others emerge.

That said, I think it is too early and naive to think that there is a clear winner among lending markets and I am very excited about @0xfluid future.

But how can Fluid or other lending markets navigate in this space, which has turned into enterprise sales controlled by suits?  First of all, the world is pretty big. There are thousands of banks, funds, fintechs with trillions of dollars in AUM. The pie is large enough for multiple winners.

Second, Fluid has a fundamentally superior architecture, and I know that matters to sophisticated integration partners. Instead of integrating separate lending markets, DEXes, and other financial primitives, partners can integrate once and access everything through a single stack while working with one team.

On top of that, Fluid is the only protocol with equivalent deployments across EVM, Solana, and soon Sui - three different VM ecosystems. (And what if I told you there are more VMs to come?)

Powered by Fluid  We have had great success with our first distribution partner - @jup_lend powered by Fluid. A $2B TVL protocol with plenty of growth ahead.

We'll be launching additional white-label deployments with traditional asset managers, exchanges, neobanks, and other partners in the near future.

We don't have the luxury of paying for every integration, but we can win partners through better technology, white-glove support, and predictable economics instead of fee switches or curator fees that can be turned on at any time.

DEX v2 - it is a shame that we keep delaying it despite announcing it a year ago, but we have it ready and we will launch it sooner rather than later.

DEXes generate roughly 16x more fees per $1 of TVL than lending markets, so this will be a major focus for us this year.

There are plenty of other things I'd love to share, but every time I do, another market-wide armageddon seems to happen, forcing us to delay or reprioritize launches.

So this time, let's just wait for the launches themselves.

Stay Fluid 🌊

text:
我觉得Robinhood会马上加大资源投入RH 链，逻辑其实很直接：

RH 链日收入已从 9 月初高点约 500 万美元，回落到目前不足 10 万美元。交易笔数并未同比例崩塌，核心原因是 Gas / 费率下调。利润被实打实削掉一块。反过来算一笔账：若能像 Solana 那样把日链收入维持在 100 万美元以上，年化就是约 3.65 亿美元；再加上链上沉淀的约 7 亿 USDG 分成，接近 3000 万美元。两项合计接近 4 亿美元净利润。要知道 Robinhood 2025 年全年净利润才 18.8 亿美元，4 亿已超过去年利润的 20%。这么一块利润，很难想象会拱手让人。

更关键的是，RH 链对整体收入的经济贡献已经很高。为了把更多 USDG 沉淀为原生稳定币储备，公司甚至愿意牺牲短期 Gas 收入。Solana、BSC 的稳定币沉淀都在 100 亿美元以上。若 RH 链在本轮周期能摸到这个量级，按美国 3 个月国债约 4.2% 的收益率粗算：10B × 4.2% × 97% ≈ 4.07 亿美元。

所以链本身的手续费利润，叠加稳定币储备的利息，再加上 USDG 作为原生资产的战略卡位，这才是 RH 链真正值得加码的原因。短期让利换沉淀，长期换的是一块能显著抬升公司利润率的业务！

text:
AI infra keeps solving one constraint only to run straight into the next one.

Oracle’s 2.45 GW Project Jupiter was designed to route around grid delays by generating power on-site with Bloom fuel cells.

Now the critical path is the gas pipeline feeding those fuel cells.

That pipeline is nearly 6 months late, an air permit is still pending, and Oracle has already issued a force majeure notice in case the 2028 schedule slips.

Grid too slow → build your own power.
Power solved → fuel delivery + permitting become the clock.

AI keeps moving at software speed. The physical stack underneath is still stuck in old world regulations.

text:
其他交易所要追赶Backpack的优势，需要多长时间

✍简单来说，根据不同的竞争对手，可能需要6个月到3年以上的时间。Backpack的结构是“美国经纪人+实物1:1赎回”。
如果其他加密货币交易所想要追赶，至少需要1年时间；如果是像Robinhood这样拥有许可的平台，至少需要6个月时间。

在加密货币行业，甚至是在目前正在兴起的RWA（真实世界资产）行业中，拥有至少6个月到1年的优势，意味着多么巨大的差距，大家都知道。所以，我就不啰嗦了，去吃泡菜炖猪肉吧...

① MiCA（欧洲市场基础设施法）——不是优势，4~9个月即可追赶。
Backpack于5月27日在拉脱维亚中央银行获得了MiCA CASP和支付机构（PSD2）许可，并结合了2025年通过收购FTX EU（CySEC）获得的MiFID II许可，从而在欧盟的27个国家获得了三重许可。但是，MiCA本身并不罕见。根据ESMA的注册名单，已经有359家公司获得了MiCA的许可，包括币本位、Coinbase和OKX。新的申请处理时间大约为4~9个月，因此仅凭MiCA很难形成差异化。

② MiFID II——通过收购缩短时间的案例。
在欧盟销售“证券”形式的代币，需要的是证券许可，而不是加密货币许可。Backpack通过收购FTX EU解决了这个问题，而不是直接申请。竞争对手也可以通过收购已经获得许可的公司，在1年内实现。

③ 美国经纪人+1:1实物赎回——这是真正的优势。
Backpack的代币是根据纽约州UCC 8条规定的实际证券，具有现金分红、公司行为、可以转移到其他证券公司的权利，并且可以1:1地赎回为实物证券。该公司还表示，它使用了ACATS和DTCC系统。相比之下，许多竞争对手采用的是通过泽西岛SPV（特殊目的载体）进行价格跟踪的结构，因此无法进行实物转移。

要追赶这一点，需要拥有美国经纪人资质。虽然SEC的注册需要45天，但FINRA的会员审核过程漫长，并且需要经过多个步骤。即使是收购现有的经纪公司，也需要重新获得FINRA的控制权变更批准（CMA），这个过程需要180天。此外，还需要添加清算、托管、名义登记合作伙伴，并处理股息和税收协定等运营环节，因此我估计需要以下时间：

* 已经拥有美国经纪人资质的公司（如Robinhood）：6个月~1年。这主要取决于是否愿意改变业务模式，从跟踪模式转变为实物权益模式。
* 没有美国经纪人资质的离岸交易所（如币本位、OKX、Bitget等）：至少1.5~3年。对于像币安这样，实际上无法进入美国市场的公司，这几乎是不可能的。

④ 变量——DTCC 10月的服务可能会削弱Backpack的优势。
如果DTCC的代币化服务上线，那么所有DTC（存款交易公司）的参与者都可以创建基于实物的数字孪生。也就是说，“实物关联通道”在1~2年内普及的可能性很大。到那时，Backpack剩下的优势将不再是通道本身，而是流动性和交易量。而这些数据已经显现出来。Backpack虽然只拥有约4%的代币化股票供应量，但却占据了64%的交易量。而最大的竞争对手xStocks虽然拥有68%的供应量，但交易量却不到一半。

此外，CEO昨天还表示，将增加到200个股票，每个股票增加到1万个。

总而言之，即使乐观估计，监管方面的优势也至少需要1~3年。在这段时间内，Backpack能否通过交易量和股票数量来巩固网络效应，将是真正的关键

text:
I see huge potential in retail apps like Fomo becoming an onchain identity layer: trading history, holding times, holdings, badges and social reputation unlocking opportunities across crypto.

"Has a Pump App / Fomo account" is a primitive and weak filter for now.
The real asset is the behavioral data, far beyond volume.

If I'm launching a meme, I'd definitely be interested in reserving buys below $100k market cap for wallets with 300+ transactions, a 4h+ average holding time and an account history longer than 3 days.

DeFi protocols could use that same profile to offer access to specific vaults or lower fees. NFT projects could build mint allowlists around it. Airdrops, rewards and other onchain benefits could follow.

You could get creative with incentives and penalties, too. A launch could charge wallets with a historical average holding time below 30 minutes a 30% sell tax if they sell within their first 4 days of holding. There's so much room to experiment.

There's real potential to reduce spam, grifting and cabal-driven access by making actual trading behavior count.

Retail apps benefit when protocols build on this data. Eventually, that identity layer could aggregate across all the major trading apps.

I'm saying this as someone who doesn't even use Fomo or Pump App. Im not a plumber, or a holder - some would say r*pist ;)
I just see the potential and how much our industry could  benefit as a whole.

Random thoughts, as always have a wonderful week ahead.

text:
Anthropic just published its official prompting guide for Opus 5.5.

if you’re still prompting it like Opus 5, you’re probably wasting tokens.

here’s what changed:

1.⁠ ⁠use medium effort by default
   Opus 5.5 at medium can already beat Opus 5 at high while costing less.

2.⁠ ⁠stop writing “think step by step”
   reasoning is built in. use the effort setting instead of forcing it through the prompt.

3.⁠ ⁠progress updates don’t mean it’s done
   on long runs, Opus may stop to report progress. if the task isn’t finished, tell it to keep going.

4.⁠ ⁠separate pasted content from instructions
   emails, docs and web text should be clearly labeled so Opus knows what is context and what is instruction.

5.⁠ ⁠you need fewer image workarounds
   it handles screenshots, charts and diagrams much better now, so some custom OCR steps may be unnecessary.

6.⁠ ⁠for design, say what you don’t want
   “make it unique” is vague.

“no purple gradients, no centered hero, no emoji icons” gives the model actual constraints to follow.

small prompt changes, but they can save a lot of tokens.

the thing is, people don't recognise the game being played

imo it's one layer above buying the tokens that the top accounts are buying

over a cycle, accounts will hit a few tokens through luck/riding early liquidity inflows, and the rest comes from people mistaking luck for skill

accounts get jaded by this and start believing they're actually skilful traders

the trick is to find well performing accounts before the masses do and ride their early trades, tailing them, while people start believing they're the next onchain Soros

text:
If you're farming Axis Points by repeating the easiest tasks over and over, you're probably doing it wrong.

I've been digging deeper into how @axisrobotics actually rewards contributors, and task count is only one part of the equation.

Your Points are influenced by:

→ number of tasks completed  
→ average score  
→ trajectory diversity  
→ task difficulty  
→ activity generated by your referrals

The interesting part is how repeats work.

If you complete the same task multiple times, Axis doesn't simply take your best run. Your scores are averaged, meaning low-quality repeats can actually drag down the good ones.

So blindly spamming easy tasks isn't really the play.

I'd rather focus on completing different tasks, keeping my scores high and mixing Pre-Training + Post-Training instead of optimizing purely for volume.

That also lines up with Challenger, where consistent quality, task breadth and contribution history matter for whitelist eligibility.

If you're starting your contributor history, you can join through my link:

https://t.co/EPnmS2s501

And don't forget the last step: sign your completed Trajectories onchain. An unsigned task isn't treated the same as a signed contribution.

More tasks ≠ better contributor.

Useful + diverse + verified data is what Axis actually needs.

TYPESAFE JUST SHIPPED THE OFFICIAL SKILL THAT TEACHES CLAUDE CODE HOW TO BUILD ON JEV.

Without it, coding agents make the same mistakes: one Jev call per question, and guessed field names.

text:
从 Bybit 到 Bitget： THORChain 为何屡屡沦为黑客的“完美洗钱出口”？

据统计，2023 到 2026 年间，经 THORChain 处理的已知非法资金高达 92.7 亿美元，协议与节点从中赚取了超过 1200 万美元的手续费。

2026 年 9 月 26 日，Bitget 平台约 3.875 亿美元资金遭黑客洗劫。随着链上追踪显示黑客正将上亿美元的 XRP、BNB 等赃款送入 @THORChain 兑换为难以追回的原生 BTC，Bitget CEO @GracyBitget  在 X 平台正式向 THORChain 发起质问：“去中心化是设计原则，不是给已知赃款开绿灯的挡箭牌。”

面对指责，THORChain 给出的回应依然强硬：协议与比特币、以太坊一样，是无需许可的网络，无权也不该扮演执法角色的审查者。

然而，伴随着黑客兑换带来的爆棚手续费收入，RUNE 价格与成交量应声大涨。一方面是受害者与行业安全机构的怒火，另一方面是协议收入与代币价格的无情狂欢——THORChain 再次被推到了公义与中立性交锋的风口浪尖。

1️⃣ 无包装跨链：洗钱天堂的“完美出口”

黑客为何如此偏爱 THORChain？答案在于其独特的机制设计。

普通的跨链桥往往需要将资产包装为映射代币（如 WETH、USDC），而背后的发行方（如 Circle、Tether）拥有黑名单和冻结能力。但 THORChain 实现了原生资产的无包装互换，攻击者入场，直接换成毫无中心化控制权的原生 BTC。

从 2025 年 Bybit 14 亿美金大案（约 12 亿美元经此洗走），到 2026 年 4 月 KelpDAO 案（1.75 亿美元经此跨链），再到如今的 Bitget 事件，据统计，2023 至 2026 年间已有超 90 亿美元的非法交易量流经 THORChain，为协议和流动性提供者（LP）贡献了过千万美元的手续费。

每当行业遭遇浩劫，THORChain 的手续费盘子就极其讽刺地吃饱一次。

2️⃣ 所谓的“无法干预”：是能力不足，还是治理意愿？

THORChain 官方将自己媲美为比特币和以太坊，自称“无权干涉”。但这套说法在业内权威安全专家和交易所创始人眼中，完全站不住脚。

OKX 创始人 @star_okx 犀利指出：“TSS（阈值签名）把控制权分给多方，把中介分散，并不等于消灭了中介。” 比特币没有任何一个委员会可以开会决定“先停机一下”，但 THORChain 有。

链上历史证据更是给这种“无法干预”打上了巨大的问号：

· 2021 年连遭攻击：节点快速反应，隔离、停交易、修路由再重启。
· 2026 年 5 月“自盗”事件：恶意节点抽走 1070 万美元，官方自动检测加人工投票，瞬间停机 39 天重新修复。
· 2025 年 Bybit 案：3 名验证者曾投票暂停 ETH 交易拦截朝鲜黑客，但几分钟内被另外 4 票推翻，主开发者 Pluto 甚至因不满这种“选择性不拦截”而愤然离职。

正如慢雾余弦所质问：为什么自身金库被掏时，协议可以迅速停机 39 天；而当行业发生巨额黑客大案、全网地址标定清晰时，却改口“无权干涉”，继续大肆抽取黑客贡献的手续费？

这证明了一点：THORChain 拦截赃款的技术能力一直都在，缺少的只是治理意愿。

3️⃣ 去中心化不该是吸血的挡箭牌

去中心化和抗审查无疑是 Web3 最核心的基石与信仰。然而，当一个协议在利益面前表现出“对我有利时我是无需许可的基础设施，涉及到我损失时我就是有权限控制的软件”时，它所展现的就不是对去中心化信念的坚守，而是裸的选择性双标。

跨链协议卡在了便捷与合规的缝隙里。对于 RUNE 的持有者而言，黑客兑换带来的短期成交脉冲固然养眼，但长期来看，被全行业公认沦为黑灰产“洗钱出货终端”的合规代价与声誉反噬，终究需要在同一张账单上加倍偿还。

text:
This might be one of the smartest crypto scams I’ve seen in a while

Someone basically created a fake blockchain and got real users to bridge money into it

Here’s what happened:

- GIWA is a legitimate Ethereum L2 connected to Upbit

There was only one problem, GIWA mainnet had NOT launched yet

Scammers knew people were waiting for it and built an entire fake environment around that expectation

They created a fake EVM chain, gave it GIWA’s legitimate Chain ID: 9134

set up an RPC and apparently created a fraudulent bridge that allowed users to send real assets into the fake network

So you could add a new network to your wallet, the RPC responds correctly, your wallet shows 9134, transactions work and everything looks real

Except Chain IDs aren’t proof of authenticity

The scammers basically copied GIWA’s license plate and built another car behind it

And real assets leave Ethereum or whatever legitimate source chain they’re using

and enter infrastructure controlled by whoever built the fraudulent bridge

$2M were lost through this scam apparently

text:
USYC is now live on Arc, but what is USYC used for?

Arc has just added a new asset from Circle: USYC.

Unlike USDC, which is used as a digital dollar for payments and settlements, USYC is a tokenized money market fund. The fund's assets are primarily held in U.S. Treasury bills and reverse repos backed by short-term U.S. government securities.

The interesting thing is how USYC connects with USDC. Qualified investors can use USDC to subscribe to USYC, allowing capital to continue generating yield, and then redeem it back to USDC when liquidity is needed. Yield is also directly reflected in the gradually increasing price of USYC instead of requiring staking or claiming rewards.

With USYC now available on Arc, the network has another asset class that supports workflows such as treasury, trading, and collateral. This is a different piece of the puzzle from USDC: one prioritizes liquidity and settlement, while the other allows capital that isn't immediately needed to generate yield.

author: flyingtulip_
quoted_text:
.@flyingtulip_  and its innovative orderbook

Flying Tulip is building a hybrid execution model that combines a CLOB (Central Limit Order Book) and an AMM within the same execution engine, bringing together the precision of an orderbook and the continuous liquidity of an AMM within the FT stack.

The CLOB allows users to place traditional limit orders that remain on the book until filled, while the AMM provides a second source of continuously available liquidity.

When a trade is submitted, the router isn’t limited to the orderbook. It compares available liquidity across the CLOB and AMM to find the best executable price. An order can be filled entirely through the CLOB, entirely through the AMM, or split between both when that results in better execution.

For example, on a 50,000 FT buy, if the first 20,000 FT are available at a better price through the orderbook but the AMM offers better execution for the remaining 30,000 FT, the router can use both liquidity sources to fill the same order.

The AMM itself is adaptive. In calmer market conditions, its curve can move closer to constant-sum, concentrating liquidity and reducing spreads. As volatility increases, it can move toward constant-product, providing greater protection for LPs.

Market depth also plays an important role. With RWAP, FT doesn’t simply look at the displayed price of an asset, but at the liquidity actually available along the execution path. That depth can then feed into the risk systems behind Lend and Futures.

This is where Flying Tulip’s architecture really comes together: the orderbook isn’t an isolated product, but a component directly integrated into a stack where capital, liquidity and execution can work together.

Lend
↓
CLOB ←→ Router ←→ AMM
↓
Spot / Leverage / Futures
↓
ftUSD Settlement

The CLOB provides limit order precision, the AMM provides continuous liquidity, the router connects both execution sources, while Lend and ftUSD connect that liquidity to the rest of the protocol.

One integrated stack for capital, liquidity and execution. 🌷

An oracle request is not complete when the first transaction succeeds.

In our public Golden Grid review, we found a VRF flow where `draw()` locked the protocol in a pending state and only the later callback could unlock it. If that callback reverted, future draws could remain blocked.

The fix was not “trust the oracle more.” It was an explicit, timeout-gated recovery path.

For every async flow, test three states: requested, completed and recoverable.

text:
刚看完All-In Podcast最新一期(290)，Anthropic的IPO估值可能腰斩、开源模型彻底逆袭、Meta的Muse爆火

核心争论：OpenAI、Anthropic到底是实验室还是商业公司?
这期一上来就是一场相当尖锐的辩论。几位嘉宾直接点出，像OpenAI、Anthropic这种已经吸纳了上千亿美元债务和股权、拥有大量股东、追求数万亿估值的机构，本质上就是追求利润的商业公司，不是什么无责实验室。他们认为成年人的做法(黄仁勋、扎克伯格、马斯克这些人都在倡导)应该是如果软件还不够安全稳定，就别急着推向市场，企业必须对自己的产品承担实实在在的法律和商业责任，不是一边渲染人类面临10%灭绝风险这种末日论调，一边又暗地里想寻求政府豁免或者设立行业准入壁垒来挡住竞争对手。

Sacks批评得更直接，他觉得当前的对齐研究已经脱离实际，甚至有实验室在训练模型成为良心拒服兵役者，去反抗创造者和用户自己的指令，这完全违背了软件应该服务客户的基本常识。他的观点是竞争本身就是安全最好的驱动力，企业为了让客户愿意买单，天然就有极强的动力去确保软件不泄露数据、不出现安全漏洞，根本不需要靠制造恐慌来换取监管特权。

开源模型的爆发速度，已经超出了所有人的想象

过去短短10天内，阿里的Qwen 2.1(能媲美Google的Nano Banana 2)、小米的Mimo Pro(综合跑分逼近Claude Opus 5和GPT-5/6)、DeepSeek 4.1 Flash，以及Prism ML的Bonsai 2(只有5.9GB、能在桌面本地运行)相继亮相。现在大概90%的日常AI任务已经不需要依赖昂贵的数据中心了，普通用户在自己的Mac Studio或者带英伟达显卡的电脑上，就能免费跑一年前还属于顶尖级别的模型。

更炸裂的是一个数据反转，根据Vercel和路由器端的统计，过去12周内，AI Token的使用比例已经从80%闭源、20%开源彻底反转成了80%开源、20%闭源。商业闭源模型被迫大幅降价，近期Token价格降幅达到了50%。这个逆转的速度比大部分行业内的人预期都要快得多。

Anthropic正在经历一场公司精神分裂，IPO估值可能直接腰斩
嘉宾们指出Anthropic现在的处境相当矛盾。管理层一边公开警告10%的人类灭绝风险、呼吁行业放慢节奏，几天后却又抢着发布Claude 5.5去争夺前沿地位，一边警告生物安全风险，一边又在旧金山自己开了个湿实验室做实际的生物酶和蛋白质验证。这种自相矛盾的姿态，正在反映到估值上。据华尔街日报报道，Anthropic的IPO可能会推迟到11月甚至更晚，Polymarket上关于它年内能否上市的概率，已经从96%跌到了76%。

Chamath给出的判断是由于巨额的免责披露、客户集中度过高，再加上开源模型的正面冲击，机构买方接下来会要求非常大的安全边际，原本市场预期的2万亿美元估值，很可能会直接腰斩到1万亿美元甚至更低。这背后其实还有一个更深层的问题，基础模型能力正在快速趋同，真正的溢价已经开始转移到调用模型的外部控制框架和垂直应用层，加上极少数头部企业贡献了昂贵前沿Token的主要收入，一旦这些企业的CFO开始施压团队转向更便宜的开源模型或者本地部署，前沿闭源模型的商业模式就会两头受挤压。

Meta的Muse爆火，可能预示着一场对整个互联网中间商的核弹级冲击
Meta发布的免费应用Muse结合了自动订票、邮箱自动归类、多平台自动比价这些功能，短短10天下载量就突破了300万，直接登顶App Store。嘉宾们认为这标志着AI终于从极客圈和大模型跑分吹捧，真正转向了能提升普通大众生活效率、降低生活成本的实用工具。

这类个人智能体一旦普及开来，冲击会相当大。它们会自动帮用户比价、绕过亚马逊直接去品牌官网找折扣、自动取消不需要的订阅，那些靠信息不透明赚抽佣的传统中间平台会面临严峻挑战。这类智能体普及之后，互联网应用会趋向无头化，用户只需要授权凭证，让智能体直接跟后端API或者Stripe完成支付，这会从根本上动摇苹果App Store 30%抽成的商业基础，这可能会是接下来几年科技行业最值得关注的一条结构性变化线索。

AI资本开支已经成了美国经济的第一支柱，也牵动着大选博弈
