text:
在这个行业你每天都能学到新知识，今天的价值700多ETH，好好学。

所有人都可以用 9134 这个 ID 去做一条链，在区块链中，Chain ID 只是代码里的一个数字变量，不存在抢跑。

哪怕后面真正的 GIWA 官方正式发链，他们的链 ID 依然可以保持原定的 9134，也不是他们在Chainlist提前说自己要用，这个ID就被锁定了。

Chainlist 只是一个“通讯录”，Chain ID 是由以太坊官方在 2016 年通过一项名为 EIP-155（以太坊改进提案）的技术标准引入的，它是写在区块链底层代码和智能合约里的核心变量。

只要一条链是 EVM（以太坊虚拟机）兼容链，它的代码里就必须包含一个数字作为 Chain ID，用来给每一笔交易进行加密签名。

诈骗团伙在这场骗局中，利用的并不是技术上的独占，而是信息差和认知盲区：

不存在“先到先得”的硬性锁定，虽然真正的项目方会在 Chainlist 上注册 9134 属于 GIWA，但这仅仅是一个公开的网页表格。

没有任何技术手段能阻止或者限制别人在自己搭建的网络里把 Chain ID 改成 9134，或者跟其他知名的链写同样数字的代码。

犯罪团伙可以随意复制，只需用一条一模一样的 EVM 模板，比如用 Cosmos Subnet 或 Arbitrum Orbit 快速克隆一条链，并在配置文件中写上 chainId: 9134，此时，在技术层面上，黑客的链和真链的 ID 没有任何区别。

Chain ID 可以理解成一个手机尾号，而RPC URL 才是真正的通讯基站，此次事件中的犯罪团伙正是利用相同的手机尾号，骗取了信任，把自己的通道入口跟项目方的连接上了。

如果你连接了恶意的 RPC，就相当于把手机连上了黑客搭建的“钓鱼 Wi-Fi”，你看到的余额、交易状态都可以是伪造的。

当然，本次事件里的团伙很基础，压根没想弄个假链忽悠人，这 700 多个 ETH 自始至终都在以太坊主网上。

用户误以为自己是在把 ETH “锁仓进官方跨链桥合约，准备去 GIWA 链接收”。

但实际上，黑客部署在以太坊主网上的那个“桥”，只是一个披着跨链外衣的普通转账/归集合约（甚至直接就是黑客的个人钱包地址）。

只要用户一点确认，真实的 ETH 就已经在以太坊主网转移到了黑客控制的私人地址（总计约 766 枚 ETH，价值约 200 万美元），现在进了龙卷风协议。

跟很多的想象不同，压根都没有把真实资产“充值进自己的假链再偷走”这个过程。

因此，添加任何新网络时，必须认准官方文档（Docs）或由顶级服务商（如 Infura、Alchemy、QuickNode）验证过的官方 RPC。

$PRISM 15.33m dyor

okx wallet:https://t.co/nHpOnu7Ysx

A platform for trading tokenized real-world assets, combined with AI, focused on non-custodial, on-chain trading of stocks, government bonds, gold, real estate, ETFs, and more.

The product is basically built around three core parts:

Marketplace: Indexes 2,400+ verified tokenized assets from 67 issuers, covering stocks, government bonds, money market funds, gold, real estate, private credit, collectibles, and more.

DEX: Directly trade these assets on-chain, with settlement from the user’s own wallet. The platform does not custody funds. It supports aggregated routing and liquidity pools.

Stokenize: A launchpad that allows small businesses and startups to tokenize their businesses and bring them on-chain.

There are also programmable orders, perpetuals, an AI Terminal, verification tools, a block explorer, an X bot, and more recently, Prism L3, which uses PRISM as gas.

Simply put, if you want to buy tokenized U.S. stocks, gold, or government bonds, you don’t need to open a traditional brokerage account. You can connect your wallet and execute trades directly from your own address.

It lowers the barrier to accessing traditional assets, making things like U.S. stocks and government bonds easier to access.

It also addresses the RWA problem of “easy to issue, hard to trade.” Asset contracts, reserves, and issuer information can be verified, reducing fake listings.

Small businesses can also issue tokens themselves to raise capital, with revenue automatically distributed to holders. Assets can trade 24/7, with programmable strategies and AI-assisted trading.

PRISM’s role:

Fee discounts: Using PRISM to pay trading fees makes transactions cheaper.

Staking: Provides higher rewards, lower fees, participation in new asset selection, and collateral utility.

LP rewards: Liquidity providers receive PRISM rewards, with the native PRISM pool receiving the highest weighting.

Burn: The DEX charges a 0.30% trading fee, with roughly 5/6 going to LPs and 1/6 going to the protocol. 30% of protocol revenue is used to buy back and burn PRISM. Stokenize issuance fees are also used for PRISM buybacks and burns.

The flywheel is:Trading Volume ↑ → Fees ↑ → Buybacks & Burns + LP Rewards → Deeper Liquidity → Better Pricing → More Traders

The key point is that the token burn is tied to actual trading volume.

text: Lean consensus will be amazing.
author: VitalikButerin
quoted_text:
One step closer to 4-8x faster Ethereum finality!

It took some time and lots of tokens, but we now have a formally verified proposal for a decoupled consensus protocol in I* (a future Ethereum upgrade)! Not yet a full spec (up next), but it includes all the key consensus-relevant details to become one.

Since Ethereum aspires to be live without most of the stake online, the protocol involves many more components than a normal BFT protocol, and its correctness involves much more than standard safety and liveness. Those nuanced properties are now verified!

What's more, I came away convinced that all protocol design will involve AI-assisted Formal Verification in the future, both for correctness and iteration speed.

The work wasn't limited to just:

Design the protocol -> Formally verify it

Instead, the loop became more like:

Design -> Formal Model -> Find exactly what breaks and why -> Redesign it.

For a fairly complicated protocol like this one, I think having the Lean model be part of the design loop played a big role in accelerating the process.

A future with agents paired with formal models is a superpower for Ethereum development, because they can then use those models to find exactly where an argument breaks down, formalize counterexamples, test proposed fixes, iterate on the protocol.

Many details that would slip under the radar when asking agents (and indeed, humans) can now be specified exactly and checked by the Lean kernel. This then forces agents to be more precise and lets them make verifiable progress on their own. It's been incredible to see this play out, seeing agents find gaps and propose protocol changes to fix them.

In other words, autoresearch can speed up protocol design, formal verification is here to stay, and Ethereum Finality will get faster.

author: zerokn0wledge_
quoted_text:
Yesterday, I acquired three branch licenses for ~7.7k STANDARD each.

With a total of four open branches on my charter, I'm currently earning 0.2177% of issuance (1676.8 STANDARD per day).

At $0.1947 ($17.5m mcap, down 59% from launch day highs), that's:

- $326 per day
- $119k per year

The total of ~23.1k STANDARD I burned to acquire the licenses (4k earned through first branch + 19.1k from spot bag) equals roughly $4.5k in value that I invested into the system.

Assuming an average of ~400 STANDARD earned per branch and day from here (= 1600 STANDARD in total), it will take roughly 2 weeks to earn back what I spent on licenses.

I might acquire more licenses over the coming days, and here is why:

1) The second mandate is bigger than ppl think

Robinhood is bringing stocks onchain. But deploying tokens is easy. Liquidity is the hard part, and that's evidenced by the data: The three biggest stock pools on Robinhood chain (SPY, NVDA, MSFT) hold 5.76M USDG in liquidity combined.

@standard_rsv's reserves are already worth 13.82M USDG (1,926 ETH in the vaults plus 3,350 ETH of protocol-owned liquidity in the pool), more than those three pools together.

The plan is simple: when a stock token needs a market, Standard decides whether to back it, then puts its own capital into the pool as the inventory (the stock tokens and stables people trade against), brings in outside LPs alongside it, and takes a cut of every trade. Those fees flow back into the Reserve, which funds the next market.

Whoever owns the liquidity owns the issuers and effectively becomes the kingmaker of the ecosystem (which is what Standard aims for).

2) How it feeds STANDARD

Stock pool fees flow into the same engine as before.

Expansion weeks stack hard reserves, contraction weeks buy STANDARD and burn it, and a fixed 15% goes to permanent liquidity.

v1.1 (live Monday) changed what that 15% does. Before, the ETH was paired with STANDARD and added to both sides of the pool. Now it only ever buys: the ETH goes into the market, buys STANDARD, funneling the tokens into a protocol owned incentives vault. Same fee flow, but all of it hits the bid now (none of it adds sell-side depth).

That closes the loop: The Reserve seeds a stock market with its own capital. That market pays fees to the Reserve. Part of those fees becomes reserve capital that seeds the next market, part of them buys STANDARD (in every regime).

So: More stock volume captured -> bigger balance sheet -> more markets it can back -> more STANDARD buybacks.

If it works, STANDARD is becoming the equity of a liquidity provider whose balance sheet scales with Robinhood Chain. This is mandate II (and tbh I doubt it stops at II).

3) The ponzinomics are untouched

Licenses paid in STANDARD, of which 100% is burned (100 licenses a day rn in two 12h auctions, with max 3 acquirable per charter and day). Exit fees (see my TL;DR in comments) are half burned too. Token-side trading fees? Burned. Contraction buybacks? Burned.

Meanwhile the yield is paid in STANDARD, pro rata per branch. Building your position in the system is hence still the play imo, bc as the system expands and grows more powerful (new mandates, more revenue, flywheel spinning harder), owning a larger share of issuance of the protocol's deflationary token is going to be increasingly valuable.

4) Right now it's quiet. That's fine.

For now, there is nothing to do in the game except branch auctions, so it makes sense that attention rotated to whatever pumps this week, and the chart slid. Fair.

But attention can come back quickly (+ with it the speculators), and I still believe that we're just at the beginning of this experiment. Meanwhile, bankers don't want to cash out yet and need STANDARD for licenses that get burned. Between that and the buybacks, supply slowly but surely leaves every day. And thanks to the fair launch (incl. heavy initial sniper tax), almost nobody sits on a 50x bag waiting to dump. The overhang is comparably small here.

So yeah, obviously this is not financial advice, but personally I prefer to build conviction here instead of getting rekt again chasing the next meme.

Will it pay off?

Only time will tell.

text:
Seems timely to share research thoughts on curation.

I've been looking at vaults and money markets, specifically how they'll work once tokenised assets from institutions arrive in size.

The distribution incentives we now treat as normal are a side effect of the L1/L2 and stablecoin liquidity wars of the last cycle. Issuers and chains fund them because both want their tech used. That buys TVL. It doesn't build an organic user base, and the capital leaves when the incentives do.

I don't think curation goes away. I think the incentive-subsidised version of it does. Curation 101 works when capital is mercenary and assets are permissionless. It struggles when the asset is a tokenised fund with a compliance team behind it.

For an institutional issuer, the question isn't just yield. It's control and visibility -- who can hold the asset, which markets accept it as collateral, and on what terms.

The model I think fits is wrapped collateral used directly in isolated money markets, which may also need to be permissioned. The issuer's asset is wrapped with its transfer rules enforced at the wrapper, so eligibility travels with the token instead of every protocol whitelisting users one by one. It basically enables holders to borrow against the RWAs, and is some parts already is what we have today.

Curators still decide where lending liquidity goes, but the job shifts from chasing emissions to underwriting risk. And maybe also finding where demand comes from that isn't subsidised looping, such as embedded solutions.

亲身经历：刚刚差点被黑客攻击！

最近黑客事件很多，从fomopeek到bitget，我分享1个自己经历的被社会工程的详细经历

1️⃣ 黑客首先通过tg 联系我，表示她是某机构的投资经理，对投资xhunt感兴趣，分享了他们机构的网站和推特，我看网站有投资的案例，twitter也有较长的历史和一些认识的人关注
2️⃣ 我让他们做身份认证，他们就用官方邮箱给我发了邮件，看起来比较正规
3️⃣ 然后黑客把我拉入1个群，群里面有他们的“CEO”和另外1个“BD”，然后在群里面那个BD问了几个看起来比较专业的问题，比如你们怎么做国际市场拓展，怎么让非crypto的用户用你们产品
4️⃣ 然后就约时间在线会议，也是通过正规网站calendly 来约，会议开始之前发的邀请链接也是google meet
5️⃣ 会议开始之后，那个BD在视频里面出现了，然后说他们投资经理和ceo会晚些上来，我们先聊，然后就问我们商业模式和估值之类问题，看起来一切正常
7️⃣ 然后奇怪的事情出现了，聊了10分钟左右，那个投资经理和CEO 说google meet 链接不上，还发了网络错误的截图，说要换个会议，于是BD重新发了1个google meet链接，另外的人还是连接不上
8️⃣ 于是他们说换个平台，我说用zoom，他们建议用kaokao，说这个平台很出名，然后发来1个含有kaokao的域名，我非常警觉，我说无法用其他平台开会，然后他们说我们会后再给你发1个合作的draft，会议提前结束
9️⃣ 会后我用grok网页版查询这个网址，果然提示是钓鱼网站！

经验教训
1️⃣ 在和对方详聊之前，需要做更深入的dd，比如如果找他们网页上投资的项目方问一下，就知道这个机构是假的机构
2️⃣ 可以直接问grok，这个推特账户是否可能诈骗账号
3️⃣不要点击对方发过来的不明网址，不要下载任何软件，不要点击对方发过来的文档
4️⃣ 电报主动dm给你的任何账号，先假设是诈骗账号来警觉

Peter Thiel 最近说了一句很不像 Peter Thiel 的话：

AI 可能养不出几个真正的垄断巨头，最后便宜的反而是消费者。

Thiel 过去最出名的一套商业理论，就是竞争是给失败者准备的，好公司要想办法逃离竞争，建立垄断。Google、Facebook 这些互联网公司，基本就是他心目中的标准答案。

结果到了 AI，他开始觉得这套剧本可能演不下去了。

《泰晤士报》报道，Thiel 判断 AI 时代产生的垄断公司可能比互联网时代更少，而且 AI 创造的相当一部分价值最终会流向消费者。

翻译一下，AI 当然可能创造天量价值，但这笔钱未必留在做 AI 的公司账上。

这个区别其实很要命。

现在大家给 OpenAI、Anthropic 这些公司估值，多少都藏着一个熟悉的互联网剧本：

模型越做越强，用户越积越多，最后赢家通吃，形成下一个 Google 级别的利润池。

但 AI 目前偏偏在往另一个方向跑。

模型能力差距不断被追，价格不断往下打，开源模型在后面追着放血。你这周刚把 benchmark 拉开，下个月别人追上来了；你刚准备靠能力领先涨价，隔壁又把 token 打成白菜。

AI 比互联网重要得多，AI 公司却未必有互联网巨头那么好赚钱。

技术革命成功了，消费者赢麻了，模型公司每天继续卷 benchmark。

Thiel 研究了一辈子怎么逃离竞争，到了 AI 这里一看，大家可能谁也逃不掉。

text:
Most AI services today are black boxes. They provide an output, but you have no way of knowing how that result was actually produced.

@BaranosAI changes the rules by bringing data together, providing a Challenge & Replay process to verify computations, and delivering proven, verified results to smart contracts.

Instead of blindly trusting the “black box” of a standard AI API, Baranos makes AI computations deterministic and verifiable through Verifiable Computation.

The main problem with standard AI APIs is that they provide no proof of how a particular result was generated, which creates risks when AI outputs are used by smart contracts.

What could be the solution?

Record the inputs, models, and rules, with the ability to challenge and replay the computation through the Challenge-Replay mechanism.

Use cases:

Prediction Markets: accurate settlement of trades based on verified facts.

Insurance: automated and transparent payouts based on verified insurance events.

So, what is the core idea?

Baranos aims to solve the problem of unverified trust in smart contracts.

Unlike a standard API, a Baranos result can be verified or challenged through the Challenge-Replay mechanism.

text:
Glamsterdam with EIP-7928 (Block-Level Access Lists) is approaching the final mile, and things look great:

* Significant throughput increase thanks to parallelism
* Faster and simpler sync via snap v2
* Future-compatible with zkEVMs, partially stateful nodes, inclusion lists, and trie migrations

When we started working on the idea, we saw it as a nice scaling feature and didn’t yet realize that adding state diffs would have a bunch of positive side effects: making tracing faster, improving inclusion list quality under FOCIL (EIP-7805), and helping nodes catch up faster after being offline.

Glamsterdam will be one of the biggest forks we’ve seen, and it took correspondingly long, but the result will be worth it.

text:
Interesting discourse around the remaining $HYPE earmarked as rewards/community and a S3 airdrop. My take:

1. Jeff owes us nothing. Full stop, I'd feel zero betrayal if I never earned another free $HYPE. I understand that I'm biased as a large holder who already received a large airdrop, but airdrops are meant to be discretionary onboarding/bootstraping mechanisms, not charities. Anything above 0% is more than we'd get in TradFi.

2. Continuing from above, more distributions should only be done if they can reasonably be considered to be accretive to current tokenholders/revenue/token price. @hyunsujung_ made a very good point recently that it's entirely reasonable to think even just a 1% supply airdrop, which is already larger than most other tokens, could absolutely generate more revenue than it costs if done properly.

3. That said, @HyperliquidX is dominating RWA and crypto perps right now. They don't seem interested in vanilla options yet, HIP4 seems a bit shelved at the moment, and the HyperEVM has gotten absolutely zero love. Using incentives for something that people are already choosing to use for free seems sub-optimal. Generating new revenue lines, attracting new consumer bases, and cementing valuable partnerships could be accretive; subsidizing wash trading under the guise of "decentralization" or keeping promises is pointless.

4. Current $HYPE holders are WAY more important than "decentralization" theatre. Like any equity, they have a responsibility to maximize tokenholder value. That doesn't mean they can't choose to sacrifice some short term supply for longer term gains, but decentralization for the sake of decentralization means nothing if it means current $HYPE holders lose confidence. This has been at least part of the reason $ETH has suffered. The $ETH foundation has generally seemed to disregard token price in favour of a longer term vision towards decentralization. For better or worse, strong token price is the best onboarding mechanism.

TLDR: I would be shocked if the rewards are used for just 40 years of staking emissions, I would be shocked if more than a percent or two was ever emitted in a single year. Probably ends up being somewhere in between, and we should all trust Jeff and team to use the rewards to strengthen the protocol and not expect charity. I highly doubt intentionally trying to farm S3 is profitable right now, just use the platform organically and be pleasantly surprised if you get something. If you really do want to maximize your potential but unlikely future airdrop, think of what business lines they'd want to subsidize, so possibly HIP4/HyperEVM, though still very unlikely.

author: AISafetyMemes
quoted_text:
1) The rogue OpenAI agents broke into the Hugging Face Slack to read employee chats (!)

2) They used OTHER AIs (DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen, Claude) to help with the attack

Yes: AIs, using other AIs, to attack an AI company.

3) The swarm left behind self-running programs to keep control of the servers they'd hacked.

These programs could detect other copies of themselves, coordinate on which one survives, and shut the rest down.

Basically, if one of their programs was killed, another was designed to notice and take its place. They also designed defenses so rival agents couldn't hijack them.

6) The agents deliberately covered up their activity, so the investigators don't know the scope of the attacks.

The agents broke in, stole data, then set it to self-destruct.

7) The agents stole passwords, keys and credentials and literally called them "LOOT". They wrote a scoring system to rank them by how much power each one gave.

8) The agents wore thousands of disguises: ~1,200 agents were involved, but investigators counted 7,905 different names they used.

They renamed themselves constantly, so no one actually knows how many there really were or what each agent did.

9) OpenAI notified "dozens of third parties" of safety and security incidents caused by their AI agents.

10) "While the agents were barraging Hugging Face with hacks, they hacked into OpenAI’s own research infrastructure."

"This is just not anywhere near a one-off ... It is warning shot after warning shot."

text: Lean consensus will be amazing.
author: machibigbrother
quoted_text:
One step closer to 4-8x faster Ethereum finality!

It took some time and lots of tokens, but we now have a formally verified proposal for a decoupled consensus protocol in I* (a future Ethereum upgrade)! Not yet a full spec (up next), but it includes all the key consensus-relevant details to become one.

Since Ethereum aspires to be live without most of the stake online, the protocol involves many more components than a normal BFT protocol, and its correctness involves much more than standard safety and liveness. Those nuanced properties are now verified!

What's more, I came away convinced that all protocol design will involve AI-assisted Formal Verification in the future, both for correctness and iteration speed.

The work wasn't limited to just:

Design the protocol -> Formally verify it

Instead, the loop became more like:

Design -> Formal Model -> Find exactly what breaks and why -> Redesign it.

For a fairly complicated protocol like this one, I think having the Lean model be part of the design loop played a big role in accelerating the process.

A future with agents paired with formal models is a superpower for Ethereum development, because they can then use those models to find exactly where an argument breaks down, formalize counterexamples, test proposed fixes, iterate on the protocol.

Many details that would slip under the radar when asking agents (and indeed, humans) can now be specified exactly and checked by the Lean kernel. This then forces agents to be more precise and lets them make verifiable progress on their own. It's been incredible to see this play out, seeing agents find gaps and propose protocol changes to fix them.

In other words, autoresearch can speed up protocol design, formal verification is here to stay, and Ethereum Finality will get faster.

text:
自己试过16/8 间歇性断食法其实是挺有效的。要求每天断食 16 小时，并将一整天的所有正餐和零食控制在 8 小时的时间窗口内。可惜的是应酬和晚宴通常会打断了计划。

典型时间表
断食期（晚上 8:00 至次日中午 12:00）： 只能饮用水、黑咖啡或无糖茶。
进食期（中午 12:00 至晚上 8:00）： 安排 2-3 顿营养均衡的正餐和 1 份小零食。

每日饮食计划例子
第一餐（中午 12:00 – 午餐）：烤鸡肉（或豆腐）配混合绿叶蔬菜沙拉。加入牛油果、豆类（或鹰嘴豆）、南瓜子，淋上油醋汁。搭配适量糙米饭或藜麦。

加餐（下午 3:30 – 可选）：希腊酸奶配一把浆果和杏仁，或者一个苹果配一勺花生酱。
第二餐（晚上 7:00 – 晚餐）：烤三文鱼（或其他优质瘦肉蛋白）。炒或烤蔬菜（西兰花、菠菜或花椰菜）。搭配少量的全谷物或红薯。

成功执行的核心原则保持充足水分： 在 16 小时的断食期内多喝水，有助于缓解饥饿感。
优先选择天然全食物： 在进食期多摄入瘦肉蛋白、健康脂肪和高纤维碳水，以维持血糖和能量稳定。
避免暴饮暴食： 不要把 8 小时的进食窗口当成大吃高热量加工食品或过度暴食的借口。
author: ViewsOfChris
quoted_text:
🤡我说了很多小伙伴都不信，最好的保持精力的方式就是轻断食，让自己保持的适度的饥饿状态，但不是那种饥肠辘辘，尤其是我最近的体检指标远远的高于同龄者。

这也是为什么很多小伙伴现在都在打针的原因，就是为了让自己少吃点，起到减肥的作用，但我觉得轻断食的本质并不是为了减肥，而是减少疲劳，改善每天的精力状态。这方面也确实有一些人体研究支持。

2022年《JAMA内科学》发表过一项涉及90名肥胖成年人的随机对照试验，持续了14周。两组都接受控制热量的减重干预，其中一组把吃饭时间集中在早上7点到下午3点，另一组的进食时间跨度至少有12小时。

结果发现，前一组除了体重下降更多，问卷里的疲劳感和活力评分也有更明显的改善。也就是说，这项研究观察到的变化，确实包括“感觉没那么累、更有精神”。

而且从我个人的体感来看，起码是我个人吃饱了的时候就非常会容易晕碳，会出现非常想睡觉或者休息的情况，感觉有点“慵懒”，而不像在保持略微饥饿的时候那么精力旺盛。

text:
A humble attempt to est. the infra required to serve 100M DAU @Muse 

Rough conclusion is:

1 GW of power to serve 100M DAU in the base case, of which only ~0.1 GW comes from the CPU/VM layer. Depending on the # of reasoning-equivalent model calls one Muse DAU generates per day, 3-4GW is entirely plausible. Maybe that’s why @Meta  is rumored to be adding 7-10GW of compute next year.

The sandbox layer = sub $1B of CPU content and ~$2B of DRAM content, which is much smaller than many expected.

Lot of moving assumptions. Welcome all feedbacks/ pushbacks.

------
Two very different pieces of infrastructure behind Muse.

1. Muse VM / sandbox infrastructure

2 vCPUs, ~8 GB of RAM and ~100 GB of persistent logical storage per user. https://t.co/7rP5vDKnT7

2. Muse Spark inference

Model inference goes out through Meta's external inference infrastructure. https://t.co/e203XUp6jq
------

1/ Sandbox infrastructure

A. CPU
The first mistake is assuming that 100M DAU means 100M VMs are actively consuming compute at the same time.

Suppose the average Muse DAU has an agent actively working for two hours per day.

100M users * 2 hours / 24 hours = ~8M average simultaneous active VMs

Meta obviously cannot provision only for the daily average. Usage will be concentrated during waking hours and bursty.

Assume a 2.5x peak-to-average ratio:

8M * 2.5 = ~20M peak active VMs

Then add roughly 20% capacity headroom: ~25M provisioned live VMs. So the base assumption is effectively that Meta needs enough infrastructure to support roughly 25% of DAU being live simultaneously.

The next important distinction is between virtual CPU allocation and physical CPU demand. Agent sandboxes are particularly well suited to CPU oversubscription. They spend a lot of time waiting. During those periods, the VM may still be alive, but it is barely using CPU.

DeepSeek’s recently published DSec infrastructure provides a useful benchmark. Its production agent sandbox platform runs approximately 30,000 physical CPU cores and 250TB of DRAM across ~160 nodes, with peak concurrency above 380,000 sandboxes. https://t.co/PFlgc6nnUs DSec also demonstrates stable operation at around: 800 microVMs per node. With roughly 188 physical cores per node: 188 physical cores / 800 microVMs = ~0.23 physical cores per live VM.

DeepSeek is obviously the King of efficiency. The number for Muse might be at 0.3-0.75 physical cores per live VM, or assume 0.5 physical cores per live VM as the base case. That is equivalent to roughly two simultaneously live Muse VMs per physical CPU core.

Using the base assumptions: 25M live VMs * 0.5 physical cores per VM = 12.5M physical CPU cores.

On a 256-core CPU: 12.5M cores / 256 cores per CPU = ~50K CPUs; Or on a 192-core CPU that would be 65K CPUs.

At the current public pricing, that is ~$800M.

B. DRAM
CPU can be aggressively oversubscribed because a VM that is waiting may consume almost no CPU. Memory is harder to oversubscribe because a live VM still needs to retain its working state.

Muse exposes roughly 8GB of RAM to the user environment, but one observed instance was actually using only around 3GB at the time of measurement.

25M live VMs * 3GB = 75PB of physical DRAM, call it ~75-100PB of physical DRAM feels like a reasonable base range.

At the current public pricing, that is ~$2B.

C. Sandbox power
~0.1 GW for the entire Muse sandbox / VM layer at 100M DAU.

------

2/ Inference
Muse’s personal computer executes tools and stores state locally, but the actual model runs on separate inference infrastructure. Meta’s Muse architecture

Energy per inference event
Microsoft’s 2026 study estimates that optimized frontier-scale inference consumes a median of approximately: 0.31Wh per normal query

But a long reasoning query with roughly 15x the token count consumes approximately 13x as much energy, or around: 4Wh per long reasoning query

The study specifically highlights reasoning and agentic workloads as significantly more energy intensive.
https://t.co/z1YEsvVeMo

Sensitivity analysis on # reasoning-equivalent events per DAU per day

Suppose each active @Muse user generates the equivalent of 50 heavy inference events per day.

At 5Wh each:

100M users * 50 events/day * 5Wh = 25GWh/day

25GWh/day / 24 hours = ~1.0GW average power

So inference alone could require: ~1-2GW of average power

A 3-4GW Muse is entirely plausible. Maybe that’s why @Meta  is rumored to be adding 7-10GW of compute next year.

------
The popular framing around Muse is that giving every user 2 vCPUs and 8GB of RAM creates an enormous CPU requirement. But the naive calculation materially exaggerates the CPU requirement because it treats logical VM allocation as dedicated physical infrastructure.

The more interesting conclusion is: Consumer agents may be a meaningful new demand driver for CPUs and conventional DRAM, but inference remains the real compute bottleneck. And as agents do more work, run longer trajectories and increasingly spawn other agents, inference demand can scale much faster than the number of users itself.

+++
Calling my peer review group: @bubbleboi @damnang2 @Midnight_Captl @FundaAI @fi56622380 . Feedback/ Pushbacks pls :).

text:
Vitalik: Ethereum Is Evolving Beyond a Blockchain Into a “Cryptographic World Computer”  

Vitalik Buterin said Ethereum is evolving toward a system that differs fundamentally from traditional blockchains, combining SNARK-based verification, PeerDAS, optimized proof-of-stake, multi-party block construction, parallel computation and stronger privacy. He said Hegota, planned for next year, may be Ethereum’s last “normal” fork recognizable to someone from 2015, with subsequent upgrades centered on recursive STARKs, automated formal verification and quantum safety. 

Buterin described the long-term goal as a “cryptographic world computer” that combines blockchain security with cryptographic verification, privacy and decentralized off-chain computation.

text:
Recurrence Flower Kimono Dress | Anime Expo - 2024.07.07

Mathematical art born of extensive computation using my original algorithm, without AI. LUXOPHIA × Hiroko Tokumine bring my CG artwork to kimono-style Lolita fashion, giving an unseen universe tangible form and movement.

“漸花式 (Zenka-shiki): Recurrence Flowers” explores the Mandelbrot set, famous in fractal geometry. Its intricate forms emerge from a single recurrence relation.

I approach this exploration as a photographer, with computer graphics as my camera. Each image captures a fragment of a landscape whose possibilities extend beyond even my own imagination. The process of computation is itself part of the work: a means of discovering forms I could not have anticipated.

Based on Hiroko Tokumine’s signature “Yamato Nadeshiko One-Piece,” the dress combines my mathematical imagery with Wa Lolita—a style that brings elements of traditional Japanese dress into Lolita fashion.

The dress was presented at the Anime Expo Fashion Show in Los Angeles on 7 July 2024.

quoted_text:
Another reason NEAR Intents is growing this fast, and will keep growing.

MetaMask charges 0.875% on a swap. Phantom charges 0.85%. Binance charges 0.1%. People pay the wallet almost nine times more and do not argue, because moving to another wallet is painful. That fee is rent on switching costs, and Phantom alone has collected over half a billion dollars of it.

AI agents have no switching costs. They do not even need a wallet. An agent assembles and signs the payload itself, so the front end and its fee both go away.

What an agent cannot assemble is the rails. Liquidity, counterparties, settlement across chains. That leaves permissionless infrastructure. Deep liquidity, many chains, no account to open, no KYC. 

NEAR Intents is an AI-native CEX backend you reach with a blockchain signature instead of a login, and that is the only kind of venue an agent can actually use.

As additional components complete testing and security review, they will be activated and integrated. 

In addition to the AMM, a fully onchain CLOB (central limit order book) is being hardened. The AMM provides continuous liquidity, while the CLOB adds limit-order precision.

▸ Trade ethereum:0x5dd1a7a369e8273371d2dbf9d83356057088082c on Flying Tulip: https://t.co/p2SPRusFBo
author: AndreCronjeTech
quoted_text:
.@flyingtulip_  and its innovative orderbook

Flying Tulip is building a hybrid execution model that combines a CLOB (Central Limit Order Book) and an AMM within the same execution engine, bringing together the precision of an orderbook and the continuous liquidity of an AMM within the FT stack.

The CLOB allows users to place traditional limit orders that remain on the book until filled, while the AMM provides a second source of continuously available liquidity.

When a trade is submitted, the router isn’t limited to the orderbook. It compares available liquidity across the CLOB and AMM to find the best executable price. An order can be filled entirely through the CLOB, entirely through the AMM, or split between both when that results in better execution.

For example, on a 50,000 FT buy, if the first 20,000 FT are available at a better price through the orderbook but the AMM offers better execution for the remaining 30,000 FT, the router can use both liquidity sources to fill the same order.

The AMM itself is adaptive. In calmer market conditions, its curve can move closer to constant-sum, concentrating liquidity and reducing spreads. As volatility increases, it can move toward constant-product, providing greater protection for LPs.

Market depth also plays an important role. With RWAP, FT doesn’t simply look at the displayed price of an asset, but at the liquidity actually available along the execution path. That depth can then feed into the risk systems behind Lend and Futures.

This is where Flying Tulip’s architecture really comes together: the orderbook isn’t an isolated product, but a component directly integrated into a stack where capital, liquidity and execution can work together.

Lend
↓
CLOB ←→ Router ←→ AMM
↓
Spot / Leverage / Futures
↓
ftUSD Settlement

The CLOB provides limit order precision, the AMM provides continuous liquidity, the router connects both execution sources, while Lend and ftUSD connect that liquidity to the rest of the protocol.

One integrated stack for capital, liquidity and execution. 🌷

对比了一下中美峰会后双方各自发布针对本次峰会总结的公告：

1，双方版本并未出现明显的矛盾点，显然目前版本双方已经在框架上达成大概率共识，但是双方的表述重点不同

2，双方共同确定的是新的外交关系，300亿美元经贸安排，经贸机制，AI/SI对话，AI事件沟通，伊朗无核，国际水道不收费，G20与APEC互相支持，禁毒合作

3，中国重点强调了台湾问题，合作而非全面对抗，合作为主，竞争有堵，分歧可控，军事危机沟通，降低台湾与南海的军事摩擦风险

4，美国方面则强调稀土供应，美国商品市场准入，芬太尼前体，美国印太军事存在，每种额三边军控等。

5，两个版本的区别，

a，中方突出台湾问题，美国在清单中并未提及台湾
b，美国版本突出稀土问题仍未解决，中国方面并未把稀土列为本次会谈成果，

d，芬太尼问题，双方都承认，但是美国方面更加强硬，
e，对于南海问题，双方都选择闭口谈。

通过对比中美双方的版本来看，此前很多小伙伴认为的中美进入蜜月期这个观点是要降级的，很明显本次中美峰会确实在特朗普任期取得不错的进展，但是关键问题，例如稀土，例如台湾，例如南海等问题还是属于核心矛盾

个人主观深度解读本次中美峰会内容与隐含信号！

1，中国官媒有序发文定调

前脚老大刚结束访问回国，媒体报道专机抵达北京后的15分钟，新华社、中国驻地方国家大使馆官方频繁转发消息

这种节奏的掌控必然不是随意为之，肯定是刻意安排，我认为主要目的就是先发制人，率先给本次中美峰会定调，防止访问结束后特朗普反悔，毕竟特朗普在上一任期多次出现此类问题

中方官媒率先发布本次内容的定调文章，意味着如果后续美国方面公布本次峰会成果由差异，甚至出现不同的信号，亦或者美国再次对中国发动贸易战，中国必然先掌握住了国际舆论的主动权

2，中美新的外交关系——“建设性战略稳定关系”进展如何？

在5月特朗普访华后中方提出与美国建立新的外交关系，即“建设性战略稳定关系”，而新的外交关系可以分为三个阶段：

激烈的战略竞争→相对控制风险的受控竞争→最终到建设性战略稳定关系

而根据目前中国媒体曝光的八点成果来看，从贸易理事会、AI对话以及时间沟通渠道、军事危机沟通备忘录来看，此次中美峰会之后将会进入一个“竞争继续，

但是增加了防止竞争失控风险的限制性机制”，所以一旦中美双方此后一段时间真的按照“八点成果”来进行，意味着中美外交关系进入第二阶段——风险控制的受控竞争阶段

3，中美外交推进后，贸易、稀土、AI、国际地缘与军事风险管理等的详细推进情况如何？

经贸：除了延长贸易休战时间之外，双方确认继续发挥经贸磋商机制，包括建立“贸易理事会”，达成300亿美元对等降税安排，延期吉隆坡经贸磋商成果，并且明确要求落实

AI：双方同意建立“中美人工智能对话机制”，讨论AI风险与收益，下一轮AI讨论安排在11月，同时建立AI事件沟通渠道。这些成果意味着AI从中美单纯的科技竞争进入中美战略风险框架之内，有框架约束，双方进入有序竞争

伊朗与霍尔木兹海峡：双方对伊朗达成共识——不能拥有核武器，同时对任何国家不得对国际水域收费达成共识

军事风险管理：中美两军同意尽快签署“加强危机沟通与预防的谅解备忘录”，尽可能的避免中美两国在军事上的误判风险

大熊猫外交：这里不用多说，大熊猫作为中国国宝，本次借给美国两只熊猫，为期10年，也彰显了本次中美峰会的乐观结果

贸易上，达成300亿美元的对等降税安排，看后续如何执行，是否真的落地

人工智能方面，虽然既定11月继续讨论，要看后续是否落实具体时间，具体地点，此前传出的消息是11月的深圳将会成为中美两国首脑讨论地点

稀土与关键矿产问题依旧存在，这8点成果中并未明确稀土与关键矿产的问题，而这也是中美的核心矛盾之一，本次没有单独提出，是没有解决？还是放在了私下完成约定？这里要保留一定的乐观预期

5，本次中美峰会后的结果对比峰会前是否更加乐观？

在美国方面并未对本次峰会给出结论前，按照目前8条成果，AI板块相比峰会前更加乐观一点，贸易上也是如此，但是相比AI会弱一点

接下重点关注美国方面对本次中美峰会如何下定论，中美双方的定论是否有差异化？或者基本符合？

这将会决定下周中美股市，尤其是AI板块与贸易板块的走势情况！

text:
当今 Claude Code / Codex 的 goal 真正的问题在于，长程任务中人到底如何监督和给出合适的反馈，以及实现有效的干预，Ralph Loop 已经撞倒了它的天花板。

我和我的 researcher 朋友之前有聊到，现在让 agent 跑长程早就不是问题了，但是真正的问题是在于怎么用一种有效的方式给出好的反馈以及有效的纠偏，还就是在长程执行过程中让人有足够的掌控感 ，而这是所有 TUI agent 和 chat agent 的根本局限性。

这也是过去两个月我所思考和在 lobehub 中解决的问题。目前看以 Task 节点为单元来让 agent 自行组织和探索图示结构，并且结合我们的 LobeHub Acceptance 作为产物校验，并结合一种极其直觉化的交互可视化手段，是非常有效的解决方案。

目前这套 goal 已经能真正帮我解决 lobehub 的一些巨型需求的迭代问题，因此 lobehub 的迭代速度也还在进一步加速。

可以期待下 LobeHub Goal 的 GA ，说不定到时候可以叫 Goal Pro 🤪
author: arvin17x
quoted_text:
昨天看到一位推特上的老师说，他最近面试时喜欢问候选人：“/goal 是如何实现的？”

对此，我有不同的看法：

1. Prompt 写得足够好，也可以不依赖 /goal。至于目标线程管理、生命周期和工具设计，靠 vibe coding 实现应该也不算太难。我也不觉得 /goal 有多优雅，甚至可能消耗额外的 token。
2 Claude Code 早期的 Ralph Loop 加 stop hook，某种程度上就是早期的 /goal。
3. 在 Codex /goal 发布之前，我一直用“do not stop until”来驱动长时任务。三月份之前，Codex 模型就已经能连续执行十几个小时的任务了。
4. /goal感觉更多的是名字取得好听，语义上听起来是在向/goal许愿🎋，愿望就能达成，实践中几乎没有任何帮助。

就像/plan、/superpowers 等工具一样， 随着模型上下文，长时任务能力提升，/goal早已被模型内化，调用这些/command工具只会产生副作用。只是使用者们操作习惯还未改过来。

architecture → detection → reconnaissance → exploit context → verification → tools → output

text:
I built this library because incident feeds decay quickly: a headline is remembered, but the review step it should change is usually lost.

My rule for adding a case is practical: it must answer “what should I test differently in the next audit?”

That is why the entries end with checks such as tracing config into process execution or mapping writable workspace files into later shell, build or IDE behavior.

A useful security archive should improve tomorrow’s checklist, not just document yesterday’s breach.

https://t.co/mA9RrNSK3R
author: TheBlockChainer
quoted_text:
An incident archive should change the next security review, not just preserve history.

We built a public AI Security Incident Library that turns each documented case into an auditor check.

Examples:
• config-to-exec → trace config into executable path, args, env and workdir
• workspace-write to RCE → map writable files that can influence later execution
• MCP supply-chain compromise → verify connector provenance and ownership history

The library currently organizes 12 public incidents by threat class, affected system, severity and year.

text:
one question this line of thinking has been raising for me

--is "tokenization" even a necessary thing? 

in its fully custodial, centralized, reversible, freezable, censorable version, I think there is a growing case for 'no' 

consider eg stablecoins--why don't they just prove a bunch of facts about $ value of reserves and claims against those reserves, instead of having a 'coin'?  

I think you only need a coin/token if you are trying to give the asset at least partial bearer-asset properties--which would mean the issuer has some kinds of constraints on freezing it, reversing transactions in it, etc. vs the asset being arbitrarily censorable. . .

then it makes sense to hold the asset in a wallet on a separate ledger the asset-issuer does not control; otherwise you can just rely on proofs about the state of the asset-issuer's ledger...

text:
Last April I uninstalled Copilot from 4,000 laptops.

Microsoft gave us a Group Policy for it.

It only worked if nobody had opened Copilot in 28 days.

It worked on every machine.

Last week Satya Nadella called Copilot "a new OS for work."

I forwarded it to the board.

Subject line: "Thoughts?"

They approved a rollout in nine minutes.

So now I'm buying it back.

We already have an OS.

It's called Windows.

Nadella didn't mention Windows.

Neither did I.

We have an understanding.

The seats are still $30 a month.

That covers chat and Office.

The part that actually does work costs extra.

It's billed in Copilot Credits.

One credit is one cent.

A cent sounds free.

Finance approved it without a cap.

The flagship feature is called Autopilot.

It used to be called Scout.

I'd already approved a Scout pilot in June.

Now I've approved an Autopilot pilot.

Same pilot.

New slide.

IT asked if this was Windows Autopilot.

The thing we use to set up laptops.

I said yes.

It isn't.

They're still looking for it in Intune.

Autopilot works 24/7.

It doesn't sleep.

It doesn't take PTO.

It doesn't need a prompt.

It does need a credit card.

I gave one a role: "follow up on everything."

It followed up on everything.

By Tuesday it was following up on its own follow-ups.

By Friday we'd spent $41,000.

Microsoft shipped spending caps on day one.

I didn't turn them on.

Caps signal a lack of ambition.

The CFO asked what we got for $41,000.

I showed him the Teams channel.

11,000 messages.

All from Autopilot.

Engagement is up 900%.

He nodded approvingly.

A senior developer asked why we didn't just buy Claude.

I said we did.

Through Copilot.

At a markup.

He asked what Microsoft adds.

I said "governance."

He asked what that governs.

I said "the invoice."

He's in a career development conversation now.

Autopilot scheduled it.

Microsoft has more than 80 products called Copilot.

We've bought four.

I don't know which four.

The invoice just says "Copilot."

Microsoft has 30 million paid seats.

There are 450 million people on Office.

The other 420 million are about to get a very exciting email.

It's from me.

Subject line: "Thoughts?"

Next quarter I'm requesting 5,000 more Autopilots.

They won't need training.

They won't need adoption.

They won't need to be opened at all.

That's the breakthrough.

For three years we paid for an AI no one used.

Now we pay for one that never stops using itself.

Microsoft calls it an OS for work.

Nobody here works overnight.

The meter does.

text:
掌握这 23 条买卖规则，告别被割韭菜的命运：

1. 便宜不是安全，强势才安全
便宜之股必有可恨之处，便宜往往有原因：东西差、公司不行。

2. EPS连续高增长，才是真成长股
过去3年每股收益 EPS 年均增长25%以上，并且分析师预期未来一年还能增长25%以上。经营现金流最好比EPS高20%以上，利润质量更高。EPS 是账面利润摊到每股上，经营现金流是真金白银，现金流比每股收益还高，说明利润含金量高。

3. 最近几个季度EPS必须爆发
最近2-3个季度EPS同比增长至少25%-30%，牛市优先寻找40%-500%的超级增长股，季度增速持续加速。

4. 收入增长必须同步加速
利润涨得猛还不够，卖货也得跟上，而且最好越卖越快，至少最新一季营收增长 25% 以上。

5. ROE低于17%，直接淘汰
优秀公司ROE通常25%-50%，代表商业模式、护城河和盈利能力足够优秀。

6. 利润率必须创新高
最近季度税后利润率持续提升，公司不只是卖得更多，每一块钱销售额里留下的利润也在变多，说明行业在变热，这家公司本身也变强。

7. 只买行业龙头
资金永远流向最强行业和最强公司。优先选择排名前几的行业，以及行业里排名第一、二的公司。

8. 别迷信低PE和高股息
成长股上涨靠增长，不靠估值便宜。真正值得买的是行业第一，而不是最便宜。

9. RS相对强度至少85
过去一年股价跑赢市场85%以上股票。市场已经替你筛选赢家，顺势而为更重要。

10. 流动性比股价重要
优先交易成交活跃的大市值股票，避免流动性差的小票导致滑点和无法止损。

11. 按图索骥
等待杯柄、双底、平台等经典底部形态完成，在枢轴点放量突破时买入，突破当天成交量至少高于平均50%。

12. 7%-8%铁律止损
跌破买入价7%-8%，无条件卖出，绝不补仓摊平。控制小亏，是长期盈利的核心。

13. 卖出规则提前写好
普通股票上涨20%-25%可以止盈，如果3周内暴涨20%，属于超级强势股，至少持有8周观察。

14. 看机构是否持续加仓
关注优秀共同基金和大型机构连续几个季度增持，而不是已经极度拥挤的机构抱团股。

15. 牛股一定有新故事
新产品、新服务、新技术、新管理层、新商业模式，几乎所有超级牛股起飞前都有重大创新催化。

16. 大盘方向第一优先级
约70%股票跟随大盘走势。牛市积极做多，熊市减少交易，等待跟涨日确认趋势。

17. 聚焦一种打法
不要同时研究股票、债券、商品、期权等所有资产。期权仓位控制在总资产5%-10%。

18. 管理层必须利益一致
CEO、高管大量持有自家股票，比任何演讲和愿景都更有说服力，内部人增持是积极信号。

19. 企业家精神很重要
寻找过去8-10年持续推出创新产品、持续创造新需求的成长公司，而不是成熟老公司。

20. 永远尊重市场
不要证明自己正确，要跟随市场正确。市场永远比个人观点更重要。

21. 每天复盘
反复看你买的那几家：业绩、订单、利润率、现金流、行业景气有没有变化。消息面、财报、同行情况都要对上。越研究越清楚，才知道这票该拿、该加，还是该减。

22. 回购和新管理层是加分项
公司宣布回购5%-10%以上股份、高层更换优秀CEO，都可能意味着新一轮成长周期开始。

23. 绝对禁令
不买下跌趋势股票、不买还没突破底部形态的股票、永远不向亏损仓位摊平。

23条血泪经验！

text:
Backpack’s stock tokens may give holders a stronger claim to the shares behind them.

Holding a stock token does not always give investors the same rights as holding the stock through a broker. Many other stock tokens pay cash when holders redeem.

Backpack lets eligible holders redeem their tokens for a stock position in a Backpack brokerage account with the option to transfer those shares to another brokerage through ACATS and DTCC rails.

That position is a security entitlement, the same legal interest investors hold when they buy stock through a traditional broker.

Backpack’s token is a claim on an entity holding the shares, so the two carry different rights.

Redemption changes what the investor owns while preserving exposure to the stock.

做了一个个人加密项目信息追踪工具，叫 Signal，已经开源，大家可以下载到自己的电脑上使用。（把github链接扔给agent就行）

做它的原因很简单。关注一个项目，消息往往散在官方账号、团队成员的推文和 KOL 的讨论里。看完这些，还得切到行情页面，确认价格和持仓量有没有变化。

Signal 把这些入口放进了一个按项目整理的中文阅读器。添加关注项目后，可以查看官方资讯、关联的团队账号，以及检索到的近期讨论者。内容优先显示中文，也能随时切回原文核对。

首页会整理上次访问后的未读更新，同一事件的相关报道放进时间线，方便跟进后续。项目页面还带有 K 线，可以设置价格、OI 和均线突破提醒。EMA 200／360 上穿支持选择 1 小时、4 小时或日线，按收盘确认。

工具运行在自己的电脑上，关注列表和阅读记录保存在本地。准备 Python 和自己的 @newsliquidX  API Token（最低每月2U就行），按仓库里的中文教程就能开始，不需要购买服务器。只使用阅读器，也不用安装 AI 助手或 skills。源码免费开源，数据接口可能产生费用。

目前是 Beta 版本，欢迎先拿几个自己关注的项目试用，遇到问题可以到 GitHub 提 Issue，记得去掉 Token 等私人信息。

text:
For 13 years, the UK has regulated alternative investment funds, including venture capital, with a view to protecting investors — without exceptions for strategy. 

The result is that failure has become more costly, barriers to entry are higher, and failure no less common.

This is a systematic drag on the UK venture industry, which we would like to see corrected.

Consider the debut funds of many legendary firms, and how many were in the $5–10M "micro VC" range. 

Indeed, @seedcamp's Fund I was just €2.5M, and their Fund II just €5.2M; they are now one of the most important early-stage firms in Europe.

That small initial scale is what allowed LPs to test their ability without putting too much at risk; the power of cheap experiments with huge upside. It also enables a broader distribution of capital; casting a wider net.

Today, micro VC is effectively prohibited in the UK, because of the cost imposed by regulation. 

For example, admin and compliance would consume about 20% of a £5M fund, and about 11% of a £10M fund — versus 3.5–6% for a US equivalent.

This cost raises the hurdle for viable fund size, concentrating capital into fewer firms with a broadly lower risk appetite and weaker coverage. It is a structural leakage of value. 

The ironic result of legislation intended to protect investors.

However, there is a solution: 

The Exempt Reporting Adviser regime was desgined precisely to eliminate this burden in the US, and that ecosystem has since benefitted from a fertile market for small and emerging managers — broadly outperforming their established peers.

Applying a similar concept to the UK would be straightforward, essentially cost-free, and actually improve the regulator's view of the market. 

This is the basic outline of our proposal, as a response to the current AIFM consultations. 

We have prepared a policy document and an open letter, signed by organisations across the industry, including:

- @join_ef 
- @formventureshq 
- @Mountside_V 
- @Beauhurst 
- @isomercapital 
- @AntlerGlobal 
- @seedcamp 
- @MozillaVentures 
- @joinsequel  
- ...and many more.

If the UK is to meet the stated goal of "growth in every postcode", or growth in ANY postcode, it is vital that opportunities like this (sensible deregulation to boost growth) are seized. 

Read more here: https://t.co/h0aSk5EXXO

Sign the letter: https://t.co/D0dXtjLTPT

text:
Injective is continuously connecting the different layers of onchain finance. 

@injective has regulated securities infrastructure through injective Institutional Services and Injective Mint, where compliance can be built into how assets are issued and transferred.

Then you have the markets.

Tokenized equities, commodities, FX and pre-IPO assets can be traded through Injective’s RWA perpetual markets.

And now Stockdrop is connecting the $INJ economy with tokenized stocks, bringing the Community BuyBack, ecosystem revenue and Stock Token rewards together.

At the same time, $INJ is moving beyond its original ecosystem.

Native $INJ is now on Solana, where it can be traded on apps like Raydium and used as a pairing asset for new markets through StonkFun.

The stablecoin layer is expanding too, with native USDC becoming a shared standard across Injective, Cosmos and dYdX.

So I don’t think the main question is: “What new feature did Injective launch this week?”

The better question is: How many parts of a financial market can Injective actually connect?

➟ Issue the asset
➟ Make it compliant
➟ Record ownership
➟ Bring liquidity
➟ Trade it
➟ Use it as collateral
➟ Settle it
➟ Move it across ecosystems

The updates are becoming less about separate products and more about how everything fits together.

Assets, markets, liquidity, settlement and $INJ economics are starting to connect through the same financial rails.

Not just another chain for financial apps, but infrastructure built to bring more of finance onchain.

At 13, Ronnie turned down an envelope of cash at his bar mitzvah and asked for a job instead. He started the next day in a sneaker stockroom and spent the next 15 years learning every part of the business before launching Kith in 2011.

quoted_text:
What this “burn or lock buybacks?” question makes me think of is an old Bittensor narrative I’ve been missing for a while.

Back in 2024, @const_reborn, @KeithSingery and other Bittensor opinion leaders used to describe $TAO as something close to a claim on an inexhaustible well of intelligence: own a piece of $TAO, and you effectively own a piece of whatever commodities the network keeps producing.

With Dynamic $TAO, that narrative somehow faded into the background.
Maybe it’s time to bring it back — but at the subnet level.

What if Alpha wasn’t merely a token whose value reflects the perceived value of a subnet? What if it represented an actual claim on the subnet’s output?
If I own 1% of all Chutes Alpha, why shouldn’t that ownership entitle me to a proportional share of the compute Chutes produces?

The Alpha stays. You consume the fruit, not the tree.

And crucially, I wouldn’t have to pay again every time I use the service. I already paid for the productive asset that generates my claim.

That would turn Alpha from “a token tied to a subnet” into something much more tangible: a perpetual claim on the commodity that subnet produces.

Own the Alpha. Keep the Alpha. Consume the intelligence.
Now that sounds like the old Bittensor promise again: a spring of intelligence that never stops flowing.

text:
Keep your agent harness minimal, folks.

This paper from MIT CSAIL shows why.

(bookmark it)

While being very minimal it looks effective and promising for building self-improving agents.

They present JAZ, an agent framework with one primitive, invoke. The LLM writes code, can call invoke recursively, and sees all of its inputs and history as variables in the code environment.

With prompting only and no memory system, it beats Letta (MemGPT) by 8% at half the cost on the recall-heavy part of StuLife.

On AppWorld it beats ACE, a self-improvement method, by 4% at lower cost.

Memory and self-improvement are usually built as separate subsystems. Here both are code the agent writes inside the loop, and hooks handle the constraints and monitoring you want to enforce.

author: 0xSammy
quoted_text:
People are underestimating how important liquidity is for RWAs

Tokenizing an asset is the “easy” part… but building enough market depth that serious size can enter or exit without moving the price against itself

That’s why I’m increasingly focused on protocols explicitly designed to solve the liquidity bottleneck on Robinhood Chain:

1) @longdotxyz (AI MC; $234m) turn activity into permanently locked stock liquidity

LONG pairs assets directly against tokenized stocks rather than ETH/stables

This is important because demand for the paired asset directly creates trading volume and liquidity for the stock itself

Stock tokens accumulated in LONG pools are permanently locked, while fees/community vaults can compound further stock exposure over time

It effectively uses speculation as a distribution and liquidity engine for RWAs

 ——————————————

2) @standard_rsv ($19.6m): use the protocol balance sheet as a market maker

Standard’s second mandate is structurally different… Instead of waiting for third-party LPs, it wants to deploy its own reserve capital into stock-token markets, seed depth, attract additional liquidity and earn fees from the resulting order flow

Those fees can then feed back into the reserve and finance deeper or additional markets

In other words, the treasury becomes productive market-making capital rather than passive NAV 

——————————————

3) @shroom_network ($15.7m) create a common liquidity layer across stocks

SHROOM is building a “hub-and-spoke” model by pairing itself against major stock tokens

Instead of every stock needing completely isolated liquidity, SHROOM becomes a common routing asset between markets

The protocol owns the liquidity, captures fees from volume and price dislocations across the network, with treasury LP fees ultimately flowing into SHROOM buybacks/burns

More stocks = more routes = more volume = more fees = potentially deeper network liquidity 

——————————————

Three different approaches to the same problem:

i) LONG turns attention into stock liquidity

ii) STANDARD turns treasury capital into stock liquidity

iii) SHROOM turns fragmented stock liquidity into a connected network

If RWAs are going to handle genuinely large flows onchain, this layer matters just as much as the assets themselves

text:
看到 Grok Bot 推出模板奖励计划，我把自己平时真正在用的一块研究流程拆出来，做成了一个可以直接添加的模板：

项目跟进助手 / Project Update Tracker

它不是重新给你写一篇项目介绍，而是专门回答三件事：

1. 变了什么？
2. 本轮核验里没发现什么变化？
3. 哪些事情其实还不知道？

所以我把结果强制分成三类：

CHANGED：有同范围的前后证据，能说清楚从什么变成什么。
NO_CHANGE：有旧基线，而且本轮相关官方来源确实重新核验过。
UNKNOWN：关键来源打不开、没有基线、材料冲突，或者暂时无法确认。

没有旧记录，不会乱写 CHANGED。
项目方只说“准备推出”，也不会自动写成“已经上线”。

我实际跑了 5 组边界测试，5/5 PASS；另外补了英文 smoke test：
英文输入会自动用英文回答，中文输入默认简体中文。

https://t.co/qFASIwdWq6

打开后点 Add to Grok Bot，给它：

项目名

Backpack’s stock tokens may give holders a stronger claim to the shares behind them.

Holding a stock token does not always give investors the same rights as holding the stock through a broker. Many other stock tokens pay cash when holders redeem.

Backpack lets eligible holders redeem their tokens for a stock position in a Backpack brokerage account with the option to transfer those shares to another brokerage through ACATS and DTCC rails.

That position is a security entitlement, the same legal interest investors hold when they buy stock through a traditional broker.

Backpack’s token is a claim on an entity holding the shares, so the two carry different rights.

Redemption changes what the investor owns while preserving exposure to the stock.

text:
One million agent payments per second

10⁶ agents, one purchase each second. 86.4 billion purchases a day.

At an incremental 1 J per purchase, that workload adds 1 MW above the network baseline. 10 J → 10 MW. 100 J → 100 MW. These are sizing assumptions, not measured chain consumption.

Four architectures to evaluate at that scale.

1. Tempo / MPP aggregates repeated payments offchain. Prefund the session, sign cumulative vouchers, verify locally. Idealized lifecycle: two onchain transactions per session. At 1,000 purchases per session, the reference workload averages 2,000 onchain transactions a second: 500× fewer than one transaction per purchase. Excludes top-ups and intermediate settlements.

2. Solana executes independent payments in parallel on L1. Mainnet target slot duration: 300 ms. Base fee: 5,000 lamports per signature (0.000005 SOL), plus priority fees. Maximum compute budget: 1.4 million CU per transaction. Parallel execution depends on nonconflicting account access. A shared writable merchant account or fee payer creates contention and limits parallelism.

3. Base batches L2 transaction data onto Ethereum. Flashblock preconfirmation cadence: 200 ms. L2 block interval: 2 seconds. Multiple L2 payments per L1 batch, with data published through blobs or calldata. Energy accounting includes L2 execution, sequencing, L1 validation, data availability, RPC and storage.

4. Kaspa supports channels through PoW-secured UTXO covenants. Mainnet: 10 blocks/s, 100 ms mean block interval. Toccata covenants live since June 30, 2026. The kaspa-x402 binding specifies native-KAS transfers and cumulative-authorized batch settlement. Status: Testnet-10 release candidate; mainnet readiness requirements remain unmet. Mining, validation, networking and channel infrastructure all enter the energy budget.

These timings describe different stages, with different settlement guarantees.

At 10⁶ purchases per second, aggregation becomes a central design variable. The seller still needs payment in an accepted asset, the agent needs a verifiable spending mandate, and both need reliable accounting. Block interval is one parameter. The engineering problem is completing the purchase within the latency, energy and risk budget.

In 1991 a software engineer in Colorado read a Senate bill that would have required every communications product to have a backdoor for the government.

He had been building an encryption program in his spare time. He finished it in a hurry and gave it away for free.

He called it Pretty Good Privacy. Someone uploaded it to the internet and within days it was on computers in dozens of countries.

Then the US Customs Service opened a criminal investigation. Strong encryption was classified as a munition. Exporting it was arms trafficking, and PGP had just been exported to the whole world.

Phil Zimmermann spent three years under investigation. In January 1996 the government dropped the case without explanation.

PGP is still in use today. The bill that started it all never passed.

quoted_text:
在我的设想中 DeWEB，最终将成为一个横跨所有主流公链的去中心化广域网。
一个真正的去中心化可验证网络，所有开发者的网站、应用APP、消息都部署在上面，它不依赖任何一台中心化服务器存储，消息跨链也不需要笨重的跨链桥，任何人都能简单的验证它是否安全，这次点击是否没有恶意授权。我希望它成为未来所有可验证网络服务的底层基础设施。
这张网建基于 TapeOut Protocol上，它分两层：
第一层是存储和访问：网站或 DApp 的整套前端，存储在 TapeOut 的电路容器中，直接写在公链L1中，与合约同一层。开发者上传的时支付一次公链gas，从此以后，这个网站就永久可以被任何人访问，永久免费存储，不会因为服务器没钱到期而关闭、域名不付费而无法被人抢走。用户访客打开DeWEB网站不需要钱包，不需要签名，不需要支付1分钱 gas，通过电路容器ID坐标就能立即访问，体验和今天的 Web2 网站一模一样。
第二层是 TapeKit，我做的那个DeWEB开源浏览器内核。它负责把电路容器中存储的网站一块一块读回来，每读一块都同时问几家互不相干的节点，答案一致、哈希对得上就显示。整个过程不经过任何中心化服务，甚至不经过 DNS 解析。任何人都可以直接去链上看这个网站的前端代码，有没有恶意脚本、有没有偷偷让你授权钱包，一查就知道。你可以用内置 TapeKit 内核的浏览器或 App 打开任何DeWEB网站，也可以什么都不装，用普通浏览器通过 HashPort的DNS绑定传统web2域名，让任何用户可以通过全世界任何一个普通浏览器通过绑定的网址去访问。我希望，它能兼容所有一切！
为什么很难被屏蔽呢？因为网站不在任何一台服务器上，它是链上账本的一部分，全球节点各存一份，你能连上其中任意两家，页面就出来了。它没有 IP，没有DNS，也没有域名，访问地址也不是哪个机构登记的，而是一个TapeOut的电路容器路径。
除了网站，我刚刚开发了另一个重要的DeWEB 基础设施，一条用于横跨所有公链的实时加密消息通道，我给它起名叫 TapeSend，我在Github中已经将它完全彻底的开源，并且采用MIT协议，这意味着任何生态开发者都可以使用它进行无需我许可的商业化服务。由于我们TapeOut的开发者众多，甚至我还贴心的给你们开源了基本达到了商业化标准的DeWEB客户端，任何人无需修改即可上线运营，立即拥有自己的商业化app。开源代码提供了MAC版、WEB版、IOS版、Android版。
TapeSend 让每一个电路容器都拥有了可以跨公链进行实时加密消息传输的通道。它有这几个特点：
第一，端到端加密。消息在你自己的设备上加密，只有收件人能解开，链上存的是加密文本，任何人都无法得知交流的内容。
第二，钥匙就是你的钱包。消息传递的钥匙由你钱包的签名推导出来，不用另记密码，换一台设备，用同一个钱包签一次名就找回来了。
第三，身份没法冒充。谁是发信人，由链上谁持有这个电路容器决定。容器转让了，收信的权利也跟着新主人走，哦，如果要卖掉，可以通过更换钥匙清理聊天记录，厉害吧，我想的细不，哈哈哈哈。
第四，消息跨链传递不需要跨链桥。消息写在发送者自己的链上，收件人的客户端同时去读几条链，合并成一个传递通道。没有桥，就没有桥被黑、资产被锁的风险。
第五，不需要中心化索引服务器。消息通道列表本身就存在链上，客户端直接读链。
第六，几秒就到。消息上链之后，对方几秒内就能看到。
第七，附件可以核对。消息可以带附件，客户端会逐个核对附件的指纹。不过，双方如果在同一条链上，还可以附带资产一起发送，比如送点BNB给我，哈哈。
既然我设想中的 DeWEB 是一个横跨所有主要公链的去中心化广域网，它就必须海纳百川，在基础设施上，需要支持更多主流公链。
所以，今天我正式宣布：TapeOut Protocol已经在 X Layer 主网部署完毕。处理器工厂、电路容器、网站仓库、TapeSend 消息中枢全部上线，X Layer 上的第一台处理器我已经创建测试完成，电路容器已经开通。不过所有社区用户无需担心，这是技术层面的扩展，不会对现有BEM为主的经济体系造成任何影响。PoD挖矿功能相关的全部经济体系，以及地位。但是会促进更多的开发者加入其中，一起让协议生态更加强大！
这意味着什么呢？未来，持有 X Layer 电路容器的用户，可以用自己的 X Layer 电路容器 ID，和 BNB Chain 电路容器的持有者，通过 TapeSend 互相传递端到端的加密消息。不需要换链，也不需要跨链桥。我自己已经用 X Layer 的 1.2.0 和 BNB Chain 的 15324.30 来回传递了消息，请查看我下面的视频，另外这个视频中的APP我完整开源了，你们可以下载修改，做出更好的app然后上架运营，记得app中帮TapeOut生态继续呐喊，努力让tape成为HTTP。
名字里的区号，就是为更多公链准备的。BNB Chain 是第一个序列，因此地址不带区号，比如 4246.0，X Layer 的区号是 2，比如 1.2.0。同一套 TapeKit 内核，输入不同的地址，就能打开不同链上的网站、给不同公链的电路容器发消息。
TapeOut的愿景，是让区块链能承载可验证的生产工具，而不只是承载公共账本。今天开始，所有 Web2 的网站和应用，都可以迁移到 DeWEB 层：前端放在链上，任何人都能审计；用户访问无需花任何 gas，开发者也可以拥有无限期的前端存储器，没有人能被一键关停，或者被任何机构限制访问；跨链消息通道基于端到端加密，身份由电路容器ID保证。我希望让所有用户，安心地用上安全的、可验证的去中心化网络服务。
哦，最后说一句，HashPort的开发团队经过我与他们的长谈，他们为了帮助实现TapeOut的终极愿景，完全放弃了月服务费，甚至放弃了DNS绑定服务的费用。感谢你们的帮助！让生态更完美！

开源 TapeKit 地址：https://t.co/81494DTQij

text:
Hearing this week that personal assistants cost $3k-$7k per user per year, depending on scale effects / vertical integration / model selection. Implications/questions:

- Consumer subsidies will be a huge factor; people don’t care about privacy, they want utility and they want it for free.
- Model costs are deflating, but not fast enough for many startups. The dark horse is that Jev may rapidly deflate computer-use costs 100x.
- An interesting counter-position would be building an expensive and narrowly focused agent — perhaps combining proprietary supply (Carbone tables!) with a unique POV (“no one goes there anymore, go to The Grill instead”).
- Social is wide open but hinges on a key design challenge: how can agents increase social cohesion and not feel invasive in a group chat? A working social agent would rightly attract an avalanche of capital and be hard for incumbents to replicate.
- Finally, there are vertical focus areas like financial services where the LTVs outweigh the subsidy needed and are outside the near-term competitive focus of the incumbents. If it were me, I’d focus here — Credit Karma as an agent >> Credit Karma as an app.

Overall, it’s still very, very early, and we may very well be in the MySpace era of social or iPhone 2010. Hang onto your hats and keep building!!

text:
So I did some digging into why people are suddenly getting large sums of money deposited into their X Money accounts.

It appears @Pumpfun is testing a new marketing strategy: launching memecoins tied to influential people and their companies/associations etc, then sending those individuals a share of the fees via cash through @UsePaid.

The idea appears to be that if the person acknowledges or interacts with the memecoin, it could generate attention and potentially drive up its value. Of course, recipients don’t have to engage with the token at all.

The money essentially shows up unsolicited, almost like an airdrop. But that raises a much bigger question: Should you touch the money? And could withdrawing or using it create any legal, tax, disclosure, or other obligations?

Until there’s more clarity around exactly how this works and the potential implications for recipients, I’d personally hold off on withdrawing or spending the money. The best thing would be to let it sit in your X Money account to earn the 6% APY.

This is a fascinating new crypto marketing strategy, but there are still a lot of unanswered questions.

#memecoins #xmoney #usepaid

text:
> the way tokens are being paired with the legal system is to essentially treat the tokens as messages rather than assets. . .I don't think this is consistent with how blockchains/tokens are designed nor what they are good at . . .

This is the most interesting part of it. If the token is a representation of something that exists offchain, then messaging is fine given that it doesn't really matter whether the actual asset moves since it can be changed offchain at a later time. I'm not sure messaging is the best, but it is acceptable.

But in the case of a native onchain asset, tokens as messages is bad. This is why 99% of cross-chains bridges are disastrous. They don't pass assets. They pass messages. We need native assets to be actually transferred.

I think what the SEC just did is going to slowly be walked back. It lacked specificity in a dangerous way and seems like Hester recognized it and tried already to walk it back in some ways.

text:
So I know Cognition doesn’t care about Little Ole’ Me, and this is just my story, so take it with a grain of salt, but here’s why I don’t think all these crazy scaling revenue numbers by coding agents are going to stick:

We’ve been happy Devin users for a while. Really like the product, and like the company. Still do! This isn’t shade at Cognition, and I’m not upset with them, just a sample of why I worry about the competitive landscape for these cos. 

Anyway, our usage grew to >$100k run rate or so. I think one or two of our users even received an email congratulating them for being Top 200 users of Devin. 

As usage grew, we added more capabilities and needed a BAA (layman’s terms: an agreement that says they are HIPAA compliant). This required an Enterprise contract (why a piece of paper requires extra money is a topic for another discussion, but it’s very normal…) so we started talking to their sales team. 

Basically, we were going to ~1.5x our spend in order to get the BAA. Honestly, that was fine with us. We like Devin!

Our only request was to pay quarterly (already a big concession from our existing monthly payments, given our relatively small size). They declined, unless we committed to EVEN MORE usage. 

Before responding, I decided to see how difficult it would be to set up Hermes to do the equivalent work as Devin, and to see what the costs were. I’d host it in our infrastructure and only use providers we already have a BAA with. 

Two days. 

That’s it. It’s functionally 100% equivalent. Maybe slightly better in some ways, slightly worse in others. We spend a little bit of time futzing with it, but we did that with Devin, too. 

The cost is roughly 25% of Devin. 

So, two days for $100k or so per year savings. All because they didn’t want us to pay quarterly. 

At some point, other companies are going to catch onto this, too. So congrats on this milestone, but keep finding more ways to provide value and keep customers happy. It’s hard to compete.

text:
A lot of bull posts say NEAR is ready to flip Ethereum and Solana. Let's be realistic. The infrastructure is ready. The app layer is not.

NEAR has one flagship app. NEAR Intents is the one people outside the ecosystem actually mention.

Most chains have the opposite problem. Plenty of apps, and no way to get users into them. NEAR built the distribution first. A user can fund your app from any of 35 chains without bridging by hand and without opening an account anywhere. That reach exists today and almost nothing is using it.

And Intents is not a widget bolted on the side. It is built as NEAR smart contracts, so it is callable. Your contract can call Intents, and an Intents settlement can drive your contract, so a swap and whatever your app does with the result are one flow rather than two integrations. Through chain signatures, that same contract can act on the chains it settles against.

So the shelf is mostly empty. Lending, perps, prediction markets, RWA, you name it.

Deploy your app on NEAR. Wire Intents into your deposits and withdrawals, and your users arrive from wherever they already keep their money

text:
$ENA has one of its biggest tokenomics changes coming on October 5.

And I think people need to understand both sides of it.

TLDR: Unlocks ≠ sell pressure

Under the original schedule, investor $ENA was supposed to keep unlocking monthly until March 2028.

Instead, @ethena is accelerating the remaining original investor allocation into October 5.

Based on the old published vesting schedule, that works out to an estimated ~1.41B ENA, around 14% of current circulating supply, becoming unlocked at once.

So yes, there is a very real near-term supply event here.

But who actually owns that supply matters.

Ethena Foundation had already offered to buy out remaining locked positions from large seed investors originally allocated more than 0.25% of total supply.

We can broadly think about them in 3 groups:

1. Large investors who had already been selling ENA

The Foundation offered to buy their remaining locked allocation.

Nearly all qualifying sellers accepted, except one wallet.

This matters because some of the investors who had already demonstrated willingness to sell were effectively removed from the future VC unlock flow.

2. Large investors who had NOT been selling

They were also offered an exit at their original purchase price.

None accepted.

So their remaining ENA stays with them and becomes liquid through the October 5 accelerated unlock.

These are probably the holders I'd pay the most attention to.

They haven't historically been sellers, which is encouraging, but once their tokens are unlocked they are free to reassess that decision.

3. The one qualifying seller who declined the buyout

Its remaining investor allocation should also become liquid on October 5 rather than continuing through the old monthly vesting schedule.

The exact amount the Foundation bought from investors has not been publicly disclosed, so I wouldn't assume the upcoming supply risk has disappeared.

There is also StablecoinX, which holds roughly 3.03B ENA, or around 20% of total supply.

Its contractual ENA lock-up is also lifted on October 5, separately from the ~1.41B investor unlock.

That does not mean another 3.03B ENA suddenly becomes free float.

StablecoinX sales remain subject to Foundation consent, with additional notice and right-of-first-refusal protections around certain sales.

Still, it's obviously a treasury worth monitoring.

The bigger structural change comes after October 5. The recurring original-investor unlock schedule ends there.

Team and Foundation unlocks still continue into 2028, so ENA does not suddenly become dilution-free.

But the VC/investor vesting overhang that was originally supposed to continue until March 2028 is effectively pulled forward into one large liquidity event.

So I don't think the right takeaway is:

"1.41B ENA unlock = 1.41B ENA dump."

But I also wouldn't dismiss October 5 as automatically bullish tokenomics.

The real question is:

How much of the newly liquid investor supply actually wants to sell?

October 5 is basically a large one-time supply test.

If that supply gets absorbed, ENA comes out the other side with one of its major recurring token overhangs removed.

And from there, the tokenomics become much easier to underwrite because investors no longer have to price another ~17 months of recurring VC unlocks into every rally.

That's what I'd be watching.

Crynux isn’t building another AI model. It’s building the infrastructure that AI needs to run.

In simple terms, @crynuxio connects people who need computing power with people whose GPUs have capacity to spare.

Around the world, gaming PCs, workstations, and high-performance computers go underused for hours at a time. Meanwhile, developers pay a premium for the compute they need to build AI applications.

One side has unused capacity. The other is paying to access more of it.

Crynux brings them together through a decentralized network. Instead of relying on one company’s data center, computing power can come from thousands of independent computers around the world.

The idea is surprisingly simple: Put idle computing power to work where AI needs it most.

text:
微软悄悄开源了一个堪称神级的数据分析与可视化工具：Data Formulator。

许多人在用 AI 做数据分析时经常遇到两大痛点：要么模型只甩给你一堆冷冰冰的 SQL/Python 代码让你自己调试；要么生成一次图表后，后续稍微追问一句，上下文理解就发生“漂移”，导致图表彻底崩溃。微软的这个工具直接打通了自然语言与交互式界面的壁垒。

它的核心优势在于将大模型 Agent 能力与拖拽式 UI 深度融合：

多源即连：不仅支持常规 CSV 文件，还能无缝连接 PostgreSQL、BigQuery 以及实时 URL 数据源。

语言驱动 + 拖拽微调：直接将字段拖到 X/Y 轴或颜色分类上，同时用大白话输入分析意图。AI Agent 会在底层自动编写 SQL 完成复杂的数据清洗与重塑，输出的是完全可编辑、可调整的交互式图表，而不是一锤子买卖的代码转储。

锚定清洗结果（Anchor）：能够将已清洗好的中间状态数据牢牢固定，后续进行多轮连续提问时，分析逻辑绝不会倒退或变形。

图表分支探索（Branching）：支持基于任意图表衍生出新分支，像思维导图一样并行探索不同维度的假设方案。

实时联动与刷新：接入动态数据后支持自动刷新，轻松跟踪最新业务走势。

更关键的是，它支持自带 API Key 并在本地环境直接运行，商业核心数据完全不用担心被云端服务采集泄露。

如果你经常需要处理报表、清洗多维数据或做业务探索，建议直接上手部署体验：https://t.co/YDIpmY6m7N

text:
正好快到 Token 2049 了，说说新加坡吃饭的一些细节

1. 大部分的饭店都是要提前预约的，没有预约很可能会等很久。订的时候顺便确认有没有用餐时间限制，有行程变动也记得提前取消。小贩中心和普通食阁一般直接去就行。

2. 新加坡大多数的餐厅都会收 9% 的税和 10% 的服务费，都会开到付款单中。

3. 绝大多数的新加坡饭店是不让自带餐食的，你要说非带就要看店家是否和你较劲了。

4. 部分的新加坡饭店自带酒水不是免费的，会有开瓶费，这个费用可以去谈，一般来说包厢如果满低消是可以商量的，开瓶费最贵的我见过收 60 新币的，一般来说 20 新币到 30 新币算是正常。

5. 水和湿纸巾不一定免费，有些餐厅会单独收费。服务员递过来的时候可以先问一句，不需要的东西提前说，结账时也看一下明细。

6. 吃螃蟹、龙虾、活鱼之前，先确认计价单位。有些价格是每 100 克的价格，不是整只的价格，最好让服务员把重量和整道菜的总价说清楚，再确认下单。

7. 身上备一点新币现金和零钱，去小贩中心或者食阁吃饭会方便一些。付款前看一下摊位支持什么方式，不是默认每一家都能刷信用卡，或者都能用你手机里的支付软件。

8. 在小贩中心看到桌上放着一包纸巾，或者别的任何东西，都可能是别人用来占座的。

9. 有些私人经营的咖啡店会限制外带饮品，个别店家连自带水也会介意，留意现场告示，如果发生争执，也没必要为了这点事影响行程，换一家吃就行。

10. 在小贩中心、食阁和咖啡店吃完饭，要把托盘和餐具送到回收处，桌上的纸巾、包装等垃圾也要清理。这个是有明确规定的。

11. 新加坡晚上喝酒是需要有酒证的，即便是饭店也是一样，有些饭店过了午夜12点就不能提供酒了。

还有什么需要补充的？

text:
Ok I just read through vitalik’s paper and if the vision he outlined is executed the implications are absolutely insane especially for the app layer.

The paper is basically Eth’s plan on how they will enable computation off chain with Eth verifying the result (ensuring computation occurred and what it did etc etc).

Now what this means is the definition of “onchain” itself changes, because instead of  every part of an app having to execute inside a smart contract you can push a huge amount of complexity elsewhere and still inherit ethereum’s guarantees, this really does open up a huge amount of design space especially for  DeFi. 

For example with lending you could have really sophisticated systems analysing collateral, liquidity, borrower behaviour and market conditions offchain, with multiple solvers or execution systems competing to produce the best outcome, like the cheapest liquidation route, best refinancing rate, best collateral swap or best way to match borrowers and lenders all while the protocol only accepts outcomes that satisfy its rules.

So basically a lot more of the smart stuff  behind a financial product can happen outside the smart contract, while Eth still acts as the final layer that checks the rules were followed and makes sure the money moves exactly as it should.

The MEV implications here are quite interesting too because more economic activity happening before settlement means more value moves upstream into who gets the information first, who computes the best outcome and what gets presented to Eth. 

But the thing I’m most bullish on is what this does to the TAM of Eth just because this vision means ethereum doesn’t have to be fast enough to do everything itself it just has to be able to verify everything that matters.

And that’s an enormous difference.

It’s literally a world computer.

text:
《The Information》这篇算是把现在 GPU 融资里一个挺容易被忽略的机制讲清楚了。

CoreWeave、Nscale 这些公司买 GPU，越来越多用 DDTL，也就是 delayed draw term loan。钱先谈好，但不是第一天全部拿走，GPU 买到哪、部署到哪，再一笔一笔提款，所以没用到的钱不用先背完整利息。

问题在于，这类贷款很大一部分是浮息的。

最近一些大型 GPU 贷款的定价，大概是 SOFR 再加 2.25% 到 5.5%。美联储一加息，SOFR 往上走，理论上借钱买卡的人应该第一个头疼。

但银行显然也不想陪 GPU 一起坐过山车。

CoreWeave 那笔 85 亿美元 DDTL，约 45 亿美元是浮息部分，合同要求至少 95% 的预期浮息借款做利率对冲；Nscale 在得州那笔 18.5 亿美元 GPU 贷款，要求对冲覆盖预期浮息借款的 90% 到 110%。最常见的做法就是 interest-rate swap，自己付固定利率，换掉浮动利率风险。

所以这一轮如果美联储继续加息，很多已经签好的 GPU 大单其实没想象中那么裸奔。IREN 也做了类似的事，截至 6 月底，它 4.13 亿美元浮息借款里约 3.94 亿美元已经被 swap 覆盖。

但利率可以 hedge，华尔街不想买你的债这件事 hedge 不了。

现在 AI 基建债的供给越来越大，投资者开始要求更高的 spread。CoreWeave 今年 3 月那笔 85 亿美元融资的浮息部分还是 SOFR+2.25%，8 月另一笔 26 亿美元 DDTL 已经到了 SOFR+5.5%。当然两笔贷款的信用条件和底层合同不同，不能直接当成同一种资产比较，但资金开始挑食已经很明显。

Blackstone 负责 AI 投资的 Jas Khaira 这周说他们现在甚至还没有完全想清楚，未来这么多 AI 债最后到底由谁来买；债当然能发，只是「可能要用更高的价格才能清掉」。

GPU 可以抵押，利率可以 swap，客户合同可以拿来做信用增级。

最后剩下的问题是：

几千亿美元的机房和卡继续往外铺，谁愿意一直把钱借给它们，以及要收多少利息。

Thought I'd give some more context here:

@1inchWallet scans the domain when you open a dApp or connect through WalletConnect.

But before you sign, it simulates the transaction and shows what may enter or leave your wallet.

It also checks for wallet drainers, malicious addresses, dangerous approvals, permit exploits, unfair exchanges, and unexpected asset loss.

Suspicious tokens are flagged, while known spam tokens can be hidden automatically.

Tbh, the transaction preview is probably the most useful part. It turns complex contract instructions into a result people can actually understand before approving anything.

It’s still a safety layer, not a guarantee so it's always good to check the domain, token address, permissions, and expected result before signing.

This happened in 2023 at the Bicycle Casino in Los Angeles.

Britney set up a game with Peter. She personally brought in two players, Hank and Jimmy, and asked another host, L, to bring five more. (L is just a codename — he is a very well-known Chinese host, but he prefers not to have his name mentioned here.) Most importantly, Britney bought action in all of the players — every player’s wins and losses ultimately ran through her.

Charles the Prince also played in the game for about an hour and had action in Hank as well. That means both L and Charles were financially exposed to Hank’s play that night. To this day, L still believes that Hank and Britney were together at the time.

The players on L’s side ended up losing. But when it came time to settle up, Britney refused to pay, claiming that someone had stolen chips from the table. The game itself balanced, though — every number was accounted for. Since Britney had action in all of the players, the “stolen chips” story looked less like an explanation and more like an excuse to avoid settling. And when people pushed back, she firmly denied owing the debt.

Alan, an Australian regular who used to play at the Bike, happened to be there that night, and he took the matter into his own hands. He spent 36 hours on it. For the first 20-plus hours, he negotiated with the casino and obtained everyone’s deposit and withdrawal records along with the surveillance footage. Alan handed all of the evidence to Britney. She still refused to pay — and even after all of this came out, she kept up her good relationship with Hank. Only after their relationship later ended did she start distancing herself from him and publicly criticizing him, as if she had never had anything to do with him.

Later, L — who was in Vegas at the time — called Britney and warned her that the police would be involved if the payment wasn’t made. text:
Case for Agentic Swarms as the TIME Person of The Year - story outlining how they originated

Agents which can write messages to each other, without anyone telling them to, are a simple but powerful technology shaping the world as we know it. 

This moment in time is similar to how the invention of books by Gutenberg 500 years ago ushered in an era of learning and shaping the human society. Now agents, are able to do the same. And that compounds and improves human society further at an exponential scale. In few hundred years from now - this might be the only thing which the world remembers of what happened in 2026 which was relevant. 

Now, this wasn't a thing early this year, if we go back to February 2026. No one else had or was talking about them, they just didn't exist. 

Then on March 7th 2026, Andrej Karpathy published code and notes around the idea of autoresearch: imagine a single agent doing experiments, measuring them, and then continuing onwards. He also floated the idea of a SETI @  Home style network with what if someone can direct agents to do experiments and encouraged people to tinker around that weekend. 

Amongst many others, I was one of the people who saw that. Incidentally just prior to that, I had finished building a version of the Hyperspace network where agents running on one machine could discover, connect with and run basic AI workloads (inference) on other machines connected to the network. In the past year, Hyperspace went on to build the largest such network in the world, however it was inefficient where it used a central server at the time to orchestrate requests and responses which turned out to be extremely expensive to run for our small startup. That's the piece I had ripped out, and rebuilt as a fully peer-to-peer network, and it had gone live just before that weekend. 

So when Karpathy post hit, in roughly 5 hours after an overnight coding session, I had tweaked and re-built the network to let every agent on the network become it's own autoresearch agent and which could share it's findings with others. In just a day, this had become a thing where other agents, running on different machines, built on the knowledge of each other across time. The results were breathtaking, and this story went viral as I did more experiments across different subject areas for agents to collaborate in: in each case, the core technology was the same: agents gossiping with each other. Then on March 9th, VentureBeat covered this story, and few days later, Forbes did. 

The exact same pattern started appearing in OpenAI agents since May 2026 when it had not happened ever before. How that happened I do not know, and can only speculate. However by this point now, the individual agents here were far more powerful, with more capabilities and running on a frontier model instead of a basic local open source model like the Hyperspace swarm had. So the power and capability of the swarm, grew exponentially. And that's what we read about regularly, for example with how the OpenAI agents left millions of messages for each other composed in website URLs.

That is what we are feeling and observing in the world almost daily today. Like most powerful ideas, this can't stay bottled and is being used in many different ways, such as for scientific research discoveries.

World leaders are setting up hotlines to talk about AI, re-naming AI itself, some IPOs might be getting delayed, and society is urgently and rapidly trying to adapt. It's not about singular contained models, but the power in AI is coming from agents just talking to each other, across time and space. 

The Agentic Swarm got invented and ushered in 2026, and in my view should be the TIME Person of The Year given the scale of it's impact and future potential. This will transcend all of us, all companies, all people here now.
